do: Gather the real parts and the M-1 numbers
how:
On the bench: the PMU with its 39-way connector, the busbars (P007), fuse blocks A and B (P001), the five MAXI holders (P189), the ten inline holders for the node (P002), nine relay sockets (P006), the 8-position barrier strip (P068), the perfboard on its M3 standoffs (P134), the wideband gauge controller, and one of each receptacle shell with its clip.
Write the M-1 space from C1 on a card: width, height, depth, and where the lowest 50 mm line is.
expect: Every part in the list is on the bench; nothing is laid out from a catalogue size.

do: Draw the M-1 space on cardboard
how: Cut a cardboard outline the size of the space C1 measured behind the lower dash. Mark the floor side, the firewall side and a line 50 mm up from the lowest edge: nothing mounts below that line.
expect: A full-size outline you can lay parts on.

how:
Low and close to the floor, but above the 50 mm line.
Connector facing down or sideways, never up.
Swing the 39-way lever through its whole arc with the connector on: nothing may sit in the arc.
Leave air under it: it stands on three M6 stand-offs (P060). Mark the three holes from the PMU itself.
expect: The lever opens and closes fully on the cardboard with the connector fitted.
caution: Do not mark the holes from a drawing: the mounting pattern is not in the record, take it off the part.

do: Place the busbars, the fuse blocks and the fuse holders
how:
Always-hot busbar beside the PMU +12 V stud, with its cover on: check the cover still fits with lugs on the studs.
Ground bus beside PMU pin 25: its 10 AWG wire to the bus must be 6 in or shorter.
Fuse blocks A and B where your hand reaches them with the dash in.
Five MAXI holders at the busbar: F30 (block A), F31 (K11 terminal 30), F32 (K11 terminal 87 to block B), F35 and F36 (the seat feeds).
Three inline holders right at the bar with their leads cut to about 50 mm: F12, F22, F23.
Seven more inline holders near what they feed: F15, F16, F20, F21 (off O12), F33 (off O10), F37 (off the O1 splice).
expect: Every holder can be opened and its fuse pulled without moving another part.
caution: The always-hot busbar is live whenever the master disconnect is closed: it must be covered and nothing metal may be able to fall across it.

do: Place the nine relay sockets, the wake strip, the perfboard and the gauge
how:
Relay sockets (P006) in a row, in this order so the labels read left to right: K1 K2 K3 K4 K11 K12 K13 K14 K15.
The 8-position barrier strip (P068) and the perfboard (P134) side by side: the wake parts on the board wire straight to the strip.
The wideband gauge controller where C1 found it hides, with its fixed sensor lead reaching the firewall grommet: that lead is never cut or extended.
expect: Each relay can be pulled straight out; each strip screw can be reached with a screwdriver.

do: Place the receptacles along the panel edge, grouped by leg
how:
One clip per receptacle, 60 mm of clear space behind every one for the wires.
Groups: L1 (L1-P, L1-S1, L1-S2), L2 (L2-P, L2-M, L2-S, L2-R), L3 (L3-P, L3-M, L3-S1, L3-S2, L3-S3), L4 (L4-P, L4-M, L4-S, L4-S2).
Beside L1-S1 / L1-S2 leave room for four more 12-way receptacles (five if engine block 02.16 was answered (a)).
Keep L2-S apart from L2-P, and the signal receptacles away from the pop-up motor bus and blower wires by 50 mm where you can.
expect: Sixteen clip positions marked, plus the spare room for the swap.
caution: A plug must be able to be pushed on and pulled off by hand with the dash in: try it with a mated pair on the cardboard.

do: Check the layout against the rules
how:
Low and close to the floor · the PMU lever arc clear · 60 mm behind every receptacle · both fuse blocks reachable · the always-hot busbar covered · the PMU stood off for airflow · no bare aluminium against a live stud.
Every wire can enter from below or with a drip loop.
Hold what CK04 found against the layout: nothing under a water path.
expect: Every line is true on the cardboard.

do: Mock it up in the car
how:
Tape the parts or their outlines to the cardboard and offer it up in the footwell where C1 measured.
Fit the 39-way and swing the lever. Push a plug onto a receptacle at each end of the row. Reach each fuse block.
Lay a tape from the node along the dash rail to the centre stack: that is the DCU tail, note the length.
Photograph it from the driver seat side and from below.
expect: It goes in and comes out by hand, and everything on it can be reached.
caution: The master disconnect is open while your arms are near the temporary distribution post.

do: Transfer the layout to the panel stock and cut
how:
Lay the cardboard on the panel stock (P090), centre-punch every hole through it, and mark the panel edges.
Cut the panels. Drill the PMU stand-off holes, the clip holes (11 mm - confirm on the clip in hand), the relay socket, block and strip holes to the parts themselves.
expect: The parts drop onto their holes without forcing.
caution: Eye protection for cutting and drilling.

how: File every edge and hole until a rag does not catch. Paint or coat the panels (P093) and let them cure before anything is mounted.
expect: Smooth edges, an even coat, no bare aluminium where a live stud will sit.

how:
Three M6 x 12 mm stand-offs (P060) to the panel, the PMU on them, connector facing down or sideways.
Fit the 39-way once and swing the lever through its arc.
expect: The PMU is rigid on its stand-offs with air behind it; the lever arc is clear.
caution: Tightening torque for the PMU mounting is not in the record: snug, and note what the PMU manual gives.

how:
Always-hot bar beside the PMU +12 V stud. Ground bus beside pin 25, within 6 in of it.
Fit both covers to prove they close.
expect: Both bars fixed, both covers on.
caution: No bare aluminium panel may touch a live stud: check the gap under the always-hot bar.

do: Mount fuse blocks A and B
how: Block A nearest the always-hot bar, block B nearest the K11 socket. Mark A and B on the panel with the paint pen.
expect: Both blocks fixed, lids open freely.

do: Mount the five MAXI holders at the busbar
how:
F30 - busbar to block A input. F31 - busbar to K11 terminal 30. F32 - K11 terminal 87 to block B input. F35 - busbar to K14 terminal 30. F36 - busbar to K15 terminal 30.
Fix each holder body to the panel so its lead to the bar is as short as it will go. Do not fit the fuses.
expect: Five holders fixed and labelled BLOCK-A-FEED, K11-FEED, BLOCK-B-FEED, SEAT-D, SEAT-P.

do: Mount the ten sealed inline holders
how:
At the bar, each with its busbar-side 14 AWG lead cut to about 50 mm: F12 INTERIOR, F22 DCU-CONST, F23 WAKE.
Near the O12 splice position: F15 ALT-EXCITE, F16 DISPLAY, F20 WIDEBAND, F21 KICK-DOWN.
On the O10 release branch ahead of K3 / K4: F33 RELEASE. On the pop-up command branch ahead of K1 / K2: F37 POPUP-CMD.
Tie each holder down so its cap opens upward or sideways. No fuses yet.
expect: Ten holders fixed, each with its label.
caution: A busbar-fed lead longer than 180 mm is unprotected wire behind a 150 A fuse: cut it short.

how: In order K1 K2 K3 K4 K11 K12 K13 K14 K15. Do not plug the relays in.
expect: Nine sockets fixed in a row.

do: Mount the wake strip and the perfboard
how: The 8-position barrier strip (P068) with position 1 at the end nearest the L3 receptacles; write 1 to 8 beside it with the paint pen: 1-7 are the wake inputs, 8 is the common rail. The perfboard (P134) beside it on its M3 standoffs.
expect: Strip and board fixed; positions numbered.

how: One clip per receptacle along the panel edge, grouped L1, L2, L3, L4: the 12, 6, 4, 2-way and DTP clips (P030), the 8-way clips (P162) for L2-M, L3-S3, L4-S and L4-S2.
expect: Sixteen clips; an empty receptacle shell snaps into each.

how: Where E13 placed it, its sensor lead routed toward the firewall grommet uncut.
expect: Controller fixed, lead not strained.

how:
Beside each relay socket: K1 POPUP-L · K2 POPUP-R · K3 HATCH-REL · K4 FUEL-REL · K11 HEAD-UNIT · K12 WASHER · K13 FUEL-PUMP · K14 SEAT-D · K15 SEAT-P.
Beside each fuse position, the empty ones included:
F1 · 10 A · Dash node, block B (K11) · LIVE · label HEAD-UNIT
F2 · 2 A · Dash node, block A (busbar) · LIVE · label DIAG
F3 · 5 A · Dash node, block A (busbar) · LIVE · label SWITCH
F12 · 5 A · Dash node, sealed inline, on the busbar - always-hot (D-462) · LIVE · label INTERIOR
F13 · no fuse · Dash node, block A (busbar) · EMPTY · label —
F15 · 7.5 A · Dash node, sealed inline · LIVE · label ALT-EXCITE
F16 · 5 A · Dash node, sealed inline · LIVE · label DISPLAY
F19 · 3 A · Dash node, block A (busbar) · LIVE · label COURTESY
F20 · 7.5 A · Dash node, sealed inline · LIVE · label WIDEBAND
F21 · 5 A · Dash node, sealed inline · LIVE · label KICK-DOWN
F22 · 3 A · Dash node, sealed inline · LIVE · label DCU-CONST
F23 · 3 A · Dash node, sealed inline · LIVE · label WAKE
F5 · no fuse · Dash node, block B (K11) · EMPTY · label SENSOR-2
F30 · 40 A · Dash node, a weatherproof MAXI holder (P189) at the busbar stud, feeding fuse … · LIVE · label BLOCK-A-FEED
F31 · 40 A · Dash node, a weatherproof MAXI holder (P189) at the busbar stud, feeding K11 … · LIVE · label K11-FEED
F32 · 40 A · Dash node, a weatherproof MAXI holder (P189) at K11 terminal 87, feeding fuse … · LIVE · label BLOCK-B-FEED
F33 · 10 A · Dash node, sealed inline on the O10 release branch (N85), ahead of K3 / K4 … · LIVE · label RELEASE
F35 · 25 A · Dash node, a weatherproof MAXI holder (P189) at the busbar stud (D-469) · LIVE · label SEAT-D
F36 · 25 A · Dash node, a weatherproof MAXI holder (P189) at the busbar stud (D-469) · LIVE · label SEAT-P
F37 · 5 A · Dash node, sealed inline on the pop-up command branch, between the motor-bus … · LIVE · label POPUP-CMD
expect: Every socket and every fuse position reads its id and name from where you will stand to service it.

do: Measure and bag every part first
how:
From the resistor kit (P069): 10 k x2 (WS01, the rail bleed), 100 k x5 (WS02, WS10, WS20 and the two bias), 220 k x2, 1 M x4, 130 k 1 % x2, 47 k x2.
Measure each with the meter and lay them on a labelled card. 2N3904 x5 (P072), LM2903 x1 (P160), 2.2 µF film x2 (P158), 1N4148 x2 (P161), 100 nF x1, 1N5819 x7 (P071).
expect: Every resistor reads within its tolerance of the marked value.
caution: The 100 nF capacitor has no parts row: take it from stock and note it.

do: Fit the seven diodes to the strip
how:
One 1N5819 per input position 1 to 7: the plain end under the input screw, the banded end (cathode) to the common rail at position 8.
Join the seven banded ends to position 8 with a bare bus wire or a jumper comb; sleeve any lead that could touch its neighbour.
expect: Diode test from each input screw to position 8: it conducts one way with a low forward reading (a Schottky) and is open the other way.
caution: A diode fitted backwards holds the car asleep on that input, or back-feeds a source: test all seven.

how: 10 kΩ from position 8 (the rail) to a ring on the GND bus, 16 AWG BLK.
expect: 10 kΩ from position 8 to the GND bus.

do: Build the shared part of the stages on the perfboard
how:
WS00 · Q0 2N3904 · base via WS01 from O22 → collector to both Q1 bases
WS01 · R 10k · O22 → Q0 base
WS02 · R 100k · Q0 base → ground
WS03 · C 100 nF · U1 V+ (F23) → ground
expect: With O22 off (asleep) Q0 is off; the 100 nF sits right at the LM2903 supply pin.

do: Build stage 1 - the door line, A6
how:
WS10 · R 100k · F23 wake supply (+12 V, constant) → Q11 base
WS11 · Q11 2N3904 · collector F23 +12 V → emitter to WS12
WS12 · R 220k · Q11 emitter → A6 line (pin 18, N44)
WS13 · R 1M · F23 wake supply (+12 V, constant) → U1A IN+ (threshold divider, top)
WS14 · R 130k · U1A IN+ → ground
WS15 · U1A LM2903 (P160), one half · IN- = A6 line (pin 18, N44); IN+ = WS13 / WS14 node; V+ = F23 → OUT (open collector) → WS16 pull-up and WS17
WS16 · R 47k · F23 +12 V → Q21 collector
WS17 · C 2.2 µF film (P158) · Q21 collector → Q31 base
WS18 · R 1M · Q31 base → ground
WS19 · D 1N4148 · anode ground → Base clamp: when the switch is released the edge swings the base about 12 V negative - over the 6 V VEBO without it
WS1A · Q31 2N3904 · collector F23 +12 V → emitter to wake strip input 3 (N35)
WS19, the base clamp: anode to ground, cathode to the Q31 base (the table's to-cell holds the reason instead of the node).
The table still calls the comparator output node the Q21 collector: it is U1A OUT, the open-collector pin, with WS16 as its pull-up.
expect: Every joint shiny; no bridge between rows (check with the meter on ohms between neighbours).

do: Build stage 2 - the horn / hazard / wink line, A8
how:
WS20 · R 100k · F23 wake supply (+12 V, constant) → Q12 base
WS21 · Q12 2N3904 · collector F23 +12 V → emitter to WS22
WS22 · R 220k · Q12 emitter → A8 line (pin 19, N43)
WS23 · R 1M · F23 wake supply (+12 V, constant) → U1B IN+ (threshold divider, top)
WS24 · R 130k · U1B IN+ → ground
WS25 · U1B LM2903 (P160), the other half · IN- = A8 line (pin 19, N43); IN+ = WS23 / WS24 node; V+ = F23 → OUT (open collector) → WS26 pull-up and WS27
WS26 · R 47k · F23 +12 V → Q22 collector
WS27 · C 2.2 µF film (P158) · Q22 collector → Q32 base
WS28 · R 1M · Q32 base → ground
WS29 · D 1N4148 · anode ground → Base clamp: when the switch is released the edge swings the base about 12 V negative - over the 6 V VEBO without it
WS2A · Q32 2N3904 · collector F23 +12 V → emitter to wake strip input 4 (N36)
WS29, the base clamp: anode to ground, cathode to the Q32 base.
As stage 1: the Q22 collector node is U1B OUT with WS26 as its pull-up.
expect: As stage 1.

do: Bring the stage wires out to labelled flying leads
how:
F23 supply in: 16 AWG PNK (N87). Ground: 16 AWG BLK to the GND bus.
A6 line (to PMU pin 18, N44) and A8 line (to PMU pin 19, N43): 16 AWG GRY.
O22 in (from pin 8, to WS01): 16 AWG RED. Stage 1 out to strip input 3 (N35) and stage 2 out to strip input 4 (N36): 16 AWG BLU - land these two on the strip now.
Label every lead at both ends as it is cut.
expect: Seven labelled leads; outputs landed on strip inputs 3 and 4.

do: Fit the two 100 kΩ bias resistors
how: On the perfboard: one end of both to a common pad for the pin 15 wire (16 AWG PNK, N39); the other ends to two pads for the pin 35 (A15) and pin 22 (A16) wires. The wires themselves land at E17.
expect: 100 kΩ from the pin 15 pad to each of the two input pads.

do: Bench check CK12, part 1: the three unknowns
how:
CK12 needs the PMU connected on pins 7, 8, 18, 19, 25 and its supply. The record does not say how the PMU is wired for this before E16 terminates the 39-way: if you have no bench lead, take CK12 as soon as E17 has landed those pins - before E19 and before the node goes in the car.
(i) PMU unpowered: ohms from pin 18 to ground and from pin 19 to ground.
(ii) Raise the voltage on pin 7 slowly: the lowest voltage that switches the PMU on; then the current pin 7 draws at 12 V.
(iii) The time from pin 7 going high to O22 coming on.
expect: (i) 200 kΩ or more keeps the designed margin; (ii) and (iii) are simply recorded - no document gives them.
caution: The 39-way is terminated once and never reopened: do not push trial wires into it.

do: Bench check CK12, part 2: the stages
how:
With the 47 kΩ baselines standing in for the car (47 kΩ from each line to ground): read the A6 and A8 line voltage at rest.
Close a stand-in for each door switch (24 kΩ + 1N4148 driver, 8.2 kΩ + 1N4148 passenger, from the line to ground) and each A8 switch (4.7 k hazard, 8.2 k horn, 18 k wink L, 33 k wink R) and watch strip inputs 3 and 4.
Do it asleep and awake.
expect: At rest about 0.166 x the supply on each line (1.99 V at 12.0 V), no wake, and the PMU goes to sleep. Any door or A8 switch: a pulse of about 10 V on the strip input and the PMU wakes. Awake, the lines read about 4.1 V and the excitation is off.
caution: Bench the door stage with the interior lamp wire (RY at battery voltage through its 1N4007) on the switch stand-ins if you can: that is the case the diodes exist for.

do: Mark cavity 1 and lay out the wire
how:
Find the moulded number 1 on the connector and mark it with the paint pen on the outside of the shell.
Lay out the spools: 12 AWG RED (P015), 14 AWG ORN (P012), 16 AWG RED (P009), GRY (P010), BLU (P011), PNK (P019), YEL (P020), GRN (P021), 10 AWG BLK (P017).
expect: Cavity 1 is marked where you will see it with wires in.

do: Learn the loop on one wire
how:
Cut 18 in. Print both labels and wrap them before the next wire is cut (PMU end reads from / to, e.g. O8 / L2-M-1).
Strip, crimp the terminal in the right die, tug it. Insert from the wire side until it clicks. Tug again.
One wire at a time, in cavity order, the list on the screen ticked as you go.
expect: A click you can feel, and the wire does not come back out.
caution: An open-barrel crimp that folds the wings into the insulation instead of the strands will pass a tug and fail in a year: look at every one under the magnifier.

do: Terminate the eleven large cavities (2.8 mm die)
how:
1 · O13 LS_ECU · RED 12 AWG · CAPPED → receptacle L1-P 2 - the swap reserve, pinned at the post and nothing in the L1 plug (D-271)
2 · O12 IGNITION · RED 12 AWG → the O12 splice: receptacle L1-P 1 (N18) and the four fused taps F15, F16, F20, F21 (N19, N20, N61, N78)
12 · O5 FUEL_PUMP · RED 12 AWG → K13 terminal 30 (N69); K13 87 goes on to receptacle L4-P 2 (N70)
13 · O4 DEFOG · RED 12 AWG → receptacle L4-P 1 - rear defog
14 · O14 LS_FAN · RED 12 AWG · CAPPED → receptacle L1-P 3 - the swap reserve, pinned at the post (D-271)
25 · GND · BLK 10 AWG → the GND bus, 6 in or less (N57)
26 · O3 HEAD_HIGH · RED 12 AWG → receptacle L2-P 2, a 16 AWG tap to DP-ICU-B 12 (N53) and one diode of the pop-up coil feed (N09)
27 · O15 COMFORT · RED 12 AWG → receptacle L3-P 2 (N17) and the tap to K14 / K15 terminal 86 (N110)
28 · O16 BLOWER · RED 12 AWG → receptacle L3-P 1 - blower, capped at L3-BLW
38 · O1 MOTOR_BUS · RED 12 AWG → the O1 splice (N08): F37 to K1 / K2 terminal 30, receptacle L2-P 3 (N105), receptacle L4-P 3 (N16)
39 · O2 HEAD_LOW · RED 12 AWG → receptacle L2-P 1 and one diode of the pop-up coil feed (N09)
expect: Eleven large terminals seated: ten 12 AWG RED and pin 25 in 10 AWG BLK.
caution: Pins 1 and 14 are the swap reserves: they are wired like the rest, labelled CAPPED.

do: Terminate the six 15 A output cavities (small, 14 AWG ORN)
how:
3 · O11 HORN · ORN 14 AWG → receptacle L2-M 3 - horns
4 · O10 ACCESSORY · ORN 14 AWG → receptacle L3-M 1 (N23) and the O10 taps: K12 86, DP-ICU-A 1 (N24), L4-S 4 (N73), F33 to K3 / K4 (N85), the capped radar tail (N103)
5 · O9 WIPE_HIGH · ORN 14 AWG → receptacle L2-M 2 - wiper HIGH
9 · O8 WIPE_LOW · ORN 14 AWG → receptacle L2-M 1 and K12 terminal 30 (N26)
10 · O7 BRAKE · ORN 14 AWG → receptacle L4-M 2 - brake lamps
11 · O6 TAIL_PARK · ORN 14 AWG → receptacles L2-M 7 and L4-M 1 (N54)
expect: Six ORN wires seated.
caution: 14 AWG is the largest wire in a small cavity: check the insulation wings close around it, not through it.

do: Terminate the six 7 A output cavities (small, 16 AWG RED)
how:
6 · O17 TURN_L · RED 16 AWG → receptacles L2-M 5 and L4-M 5, with the tap to DP-ICU-B 10 (N51)
8 · O22 KEEP_ALIVE · RED 16 AWG → wake strip input 5 (N37), K11 terminal 86 (N06) and the 10 kΩ to Q0 base (WS01)
20 · O19 REVERSE · RED 16 AWG → receptacle L4-M 7 - reverse lamps
21 · O21 START_RLY · RED 16 AWG → receptacle L1-S1 1 - the K9 coil
33 · O18 TURN_R · RED 16 AWG → receptacles L2-M 6 and L4-M 6, with the tap to DP-ICU-B 11 (N52)
34 · O20 INTERIOR · RED 16 AWG → receptacle L3-S1 8 and DP-ICU-A 2 (N22)
expect: Six RED wires seated.

do: Terminate the ten input cavities (small, 16 AWG GRY)
how:
16 · A2 WIPER_STALK · GRY 16 AWG → receptacle L3-S1 4 (N97)
17 · A4 POPUP_L · GRY 16 AWG → receptacle L1-S1 11 - the inhibitor P/N contact
18 · A6 DOOR_PINS · GRY 16 AWG → receptacle L4-S 2 and the door wake stage (N44)
19 · A8 HAZ_HORN_WINK · GRY 16 AWG → receptacles L3-S1 6 and L3-S1 11, one splice, and the A8 wake stage (N43)
22 · A16 KEY_POS · GRY 16 AWG → receptacle L3-S1 1 (N99), with the 100 kΩ bias from pin 15
29 · A1 TURN_STALK · GRY 16 AWG → receptacle L3-S1 3 (N96)
30 · A3 BRAKE_PARK · GRY 16 AWG → receptacles L3-S1 5, L2-S 3 and L2-S 4, one splice (N42)
31 · A5 POPUP_R · GRY 16 AWG → receptacle L1-S2 7 - the inhibitor R contact
32 · A7 OIL_PRESS · GRY 16 AWG → a tap on the L1-S1 4 to DP-ICU-B 2 conductor (N45)
35 · A15 HEADLIGHT_SW · GRY 16 AWG → receptacle L3-S1 2 (N98), with the 100 kΩ bias from pin 15
expect: Ten GRY wires seated.

do: Terminate the wake pin and the +5 V pin
how:
7 · +12V SW · BLU 16 AWG → the wake strip common rail (N38)
15 · +5V OUT · PNK 16 AWG → the two 100 kΩ bias resistors (to pins 35 and 22) and the 100 Ω 1 W oil-node pull-up (N39)
Pin 15 is the one MEDIUM cavity: use the terminal CK24 identified for it. If CK24 did not settle it, stop here and raise a note.
expect: Pin 7 BLU and pin 15 PNK seated.

how:
23 · CAN1H · YEL 16 tw AWG → DP-DIAG 1, twisted with pin 36 (N56); 120 Ω across 23 / 36 at this connector
24 · CAN2H · YEL 16 tw AWG → the CAN2 splice at the node, twisted with pin 37 (N55)
36 · CAN1L · GRN 16 tw AWG → DP-DIAG 2, twisted with pin 23 (N56)
37 · CAN2L · GRN 16 tw AWG → the CAN2 splice at the node, twisted with pin 24 (N55)
Twist each pair by hand along its whole 18 in: 23 YEL with 36 GRN, 24 YEL with 37 GRN.
CAN1 needs 120 Ω across pins 23 / 36 at this connector (N56): the record does not say how it is fitted here - solder a 120 Ω (P070) across the pair a short way back from the connector under heat-shrink, and note it.
expect: Two twisted pairs; 120 Ω between the pin 23 and pin 36 wires.
caution: Keep the pairs twisted right up to the connector.

how: Count the wires: 39. Press the secondary lock home.
expect: The lock seats flush; it will not seat over a terminal that is not fully in.
caution: A lock that will not close means a terminal is not seated: find it, do not force the lock.

how: One at a time, a firm straight pull on each of the 39.
expect: None moves.

do: Latch it on the PMU once
how: Offer the connector to the PMU on its panel and close the lever fully, then open it and take the connector off again.
expect: The lever closes without force and its arc is clear of every part on the panel.

how: Group the wires by where they go (L1, L2, L3, L4, relays, strip) with loose ties. Do not tape.
expect: A connector with 39 labelled 18 in tails, ready for E17.

do: Main power and ground at the node
how:
N57 · PMU pin 25 (GND) → GND bus · 10 AWG BLK
N58 · GND bus → Chassis, dash star point · 10 AWG BLK
N03 · Always-hot busbar → F30 (40 A) → Fuse block A input · 10 AWG RED
N04 · Always-hot busbar → F31 (40 A) → K11 terminal 30 · 10 AWG RED
N05 · K11 terminal 87 → F32 (40 A) → Fuse block B input · 10 AWG RED
N106 · Always-hot busbar → F35 (25 A), the holder's own lead → K14 terminal 30 · 10 / 12 AWG RED
N107 · Always-hot busbar → F36 (25 A), the holder's own lead → K15 terminal 30 · 10 / 12 AWG RED
N01, the 2 AWG main feed onto the busbar stud, is landed in the car at E24: leave its stud free.
N58, the GND bus to the dash star point, is also made in the car (bare metal, star washer, torque, cavity wax): make the 10 AWG lead with its ring now.
Ring terminals with heat-shrink (P079); 10 AWG RED (P018) and BLK (P017).
expect: Pin 25 beeps to the GND bus and its wire is 6 in or shorter.
caution: Stud torques are not in the record yet (rules torque): tighten to the maker's figure written at D1 and mark each nut with the paint pen.

how:
N21 · Always-hot busbar → F12 inline (5 A), the holder's own lead → F12 inline (5 A) → receptacle L4-M 8 · 14 / 16 AWG RED
N75 · Always-hot busbar → F22 inline (3 A), the holder's own lead → F22 inline (3 A) → receptacle DP-DCU 1 · 14 / 16 AWG RED
N87 · Always-hot busbar → F23 inline (3 A) → Wake-stage pull-ups (emitter rail) · 14 / 16 AWG PNK
expect: Each holder's busbar-side lead is about 50 mm; each load-side wire is 16 AWG and labelled.

how:
N28 · Fuse block A, F2 out → Receptacle DP-DIAG 3 · 16 AWG RED
N29 · Fuse block A, F3 out → Receptacle L3-S2 2 · 16 AWG PNK

L3-S2 is a DT06-12S, the 12-way plug (kit P115): size-16 socket contacts: P022 for 16-18 AWG, P024 for 14 AWG; wedgelock W12S.
1 · RUN — wake source · BLU 16 AWG → Ignition switch IG terminal (raw 12 V)
2 · Switch supply +12 V · PNK 16 AWG → Ignition switch B terminal · light switch E-01 common through F24, the inline fuse on the branch behind the column (D-412)
3 · sealing plug, size 16
4 · sealing plug, size 16
5 · sealing plug, size 16
6 · sealing plug, size 16
7 · Future module +12 V constant (F13, block A, always-hot) · RED 16 AWG · CAPPED → L3-MOD 1 — the future-module receptacle behind the dash, dust-capped (D-274)
8 · Future module ground · BLK 16 AWG · CAPPED → L3-MOD 2 — with cavity 7 (D-274)
9 · Washer relay K12 coil return · BLU 16 AWG → Wiper stalk D-03 WASH contact (same terminal as the WASH ladder leg); contact's other side → column ground
10 · Courtesy — glove box lamp · RED 16 AWG → Glove box lamp H-01 +; lamp − → lid switch H-02 → dash ground
11 · Parking brake switch → brake warning lamp · GRY 16 AWG → Parking brake switch C-04 terminal BR (switch body grounds through the lever bracket)
12 · Kick-down switch supply +12 V · RED 16 AWG → Kick-down switch B-32 at the throttle pedal, one terminal. Ignition-fed off O12 through its own inline fuse - never off F3, whose 5 A also carries the ignition switch, …
Each wire: strip, crimp the socket in the 4-indent crimper, push in from the wire side until it clicks, tug. Work in cavity order. Then the sealing plugs, then the wedgelock.
expect: Every contact clicked and tugged; 4 sealing plugs fitted; the wedgelock snaps in flush; the code L3-S2 is on the shell.

how:
L3-S3 is a DT06-8S, the 8-way plug (kit P101): size-16 socket contacts: P022 for 16-18 AWG, P024 for 14 AWG; wedgelock W8S.
1 · Future pass-through A · GRY 16 AWG · CAPPED → L3-RDR 1 — the radar pass-through's dash-end receptacle, dust-capped; linked at the post to L4-S 5 (D-274)
2 · Future pass-through B · GRY 16 AWG · CAPPED → L3-RDR 2 — the radar pass-through's dash-end receptacle, dust-capped; linked at the post to L4-S 6 (D-274)
3 · Future pass-through C · GRY 16 AWG · CAPPED → L3-RDR 3 — the radar pass-through's dash-end receptacle, dust-capped; linked at the post to L4-S 7 (D-274)
4 · Kick-down solenoid command · RED 16 AWG → Kick-down switch B-32, other terminal → back to the post, linked there to L4-S2 7. L3-S2 had one free cavity and this is the second conductor, so it takes the first free …
5 · sealing plug, size 16
6 · sealing plug, size 16
7 · sealing plug, size 16
8 · sealing plug, size 16
Each wire: strip, crimp the socket in the 4-indent crimper, push in from the wire side until it clicks, tug. Work in cavity order. Then the sealing plugs, then the wedgelock.
expect: Every contact clicked and tugged; 4 sealing plugs fitted; the wedgelock snaps in flush; the code L3-S3 is on the shell.

do: Fit the branch-end receptacles L3-BLW and L3-CMF
how:
L3-BLW is a DTP04-2P, the 2-way receptacle (kit P133), placed: HVAC case. Size-12 pin contacts (p027); wedgelock WP-2P.
1 · Blower motor + · RED 12 AWG · CAPPED ← L3-P 1
2 · Blower motor − (return) · BLK 12 AWG · CAPPED ← GND
L3-CMF is a DTP04-2P, the 2-way receptacle (kit P133), placed: Centre stack. Size-12 pin contacts (p027); wedgelock WP-2P.
1 · O15 comfort bus · RED 12 AWG · CAPPED ← L3-P 2
2 · sealing plug, size 12
L3-BLW 2 is the 12 AWG BLK return to the dash ground (G15).
Push the dust cap on (P102).
expect: Each receptacle pinned, plugged, wedge-locked, dust-capped and carrying its code.

do: Fit the branch-end receptacles L3-MOD and L3-RDR
how:
L3-MOD is a DT04-2P, the 2-way receptacle (kit P130), placed: Behind the dash. Size-16 pin contacts: p023 for 16-18 awg, p025 for 14 awg; wedgelock W2P.
1 · Future module +12 V constant (F13, block A, always-hot) · RED 16 AWG · CAPPED ← L3-S2 7
2 · Future module ground · BLK 16 AWG · CAPPED ← L3-S2 8
L3-RDR is a DT04-4P, the 4-way receptacle (kit P129), placed: Behind the dash. Size-16 pin contacts: p023 for 16-18 awg, p025 for 14 awg; wedgelock W4P.
1 · Radar pass-through A · GRY 16 AWG · CAPPED ← L3-S3 1
2 · Radar pass-through B · GRY 16 AWG · CAPPED ← L3-S3 2
3 · Radar pass-through C · GRY 16 AWG · CAPPED ← L3-S3 3
4 · sealing plug, size 16
Push the dust cap on (P125 on L3-MOD, P036 on L3-RDR).

do: Build the switch-supply branch and F24
how:
The L3-S2 2 wire (16 AWG PNK, from F3) runs to the ignition switch B terminal.
Behind the lower dash, butt-splice a branch off it into a sealed inline holder (P002) with a 3 A fuse: F24, label LIGHT-SW.
After F24 the branch feeds two things: the light switch E-01 common, and the brake-wake plunger switch (whose other side is the L3-S1 7 wire).
expect: L3-S2 2 beeps to the switch B end; through F24 (fuse in) it beeps to the light-switch common end and the plunger feed end.
caution: The key supply stays live with the key out: this branch must be fused where it leaves, not further along.

do: End the leg at the ignition switch
how:
New switch (P086), four terminals by function:
B ← L3-S2 2 (PNK)
ACC → 33 kΩ → the L3-S1 1 wire (GRY); and ACC direct → L3-S1 12 (BLU)
IG → 15 kΩ → the same L3-S1 1 wire; and IG direct → L3-S2 1 (BLU)
ST → 6.8 kΩ → the same L3-S1 1 wire
The three resistors are the E7 sub-assemblies: solder, adhesive heat-shrink, all three summed onto the one GRY wire.
Which blade of the new switch is B, ACC, IG and ST is not in the record: prove it with the meter and the key before joining.
expect: Between the L3-S2 2 and L3-S1 1 cavities: OFF open · ACC 33 kΩ · RUN about 10.3 kΩ · START about 4.1 kΩ (about 4.7 kΩ if ACC drops out in START).
caution: If CK10 found that IG drops at START, a diode from ST into the K13 coil is needed (one 1N5819): stop and raise a note before finishing this end.

do: End the leg at the light switch
how:
Switch E-01 on the column, kept. common ← the F24 branch
PARK contact → 33 kΩ → the L3-S1 2 wire (GRY)
HEAD contact → 15 kΩ → L3-S1 2
DIMMER HI contact, fed from the HEAD contact side → 8.2 kΩ → L3-S1 2
PASS contact → 3.3 kΩ → L3-S1 2
This switch keeps its factory plug: the joins are butt splices onto 150 mm of factory lead (see What to know for when).
expect: From the F24 branch end to the L3-S1 2 cavity: OFF open · PARK 33 kΩ · HEAD low about 10.3 kΩ · HEAD high about 4.6 kΩ · PASS about 1.9 kΩ.
caution: CK17: the 1980 manual shows PASS closing the HIGH contact, not one of its own. Build to what CK17 measured on this car.

do: End the leg at the turn stalk and the hazard switch
how:
Turn stalk F-02: LEFT → 1.8 kΩ → the L3-S1 3 wire · RIGHT → 10 kΩ → L3-S1 3 · OFF → 47 kΩ → L3-S1 3 · common → column ground, 16 AWG BLK.
Hazard switch: contact → 4.7 kΩ → the L3-S1 6 wire; a 47 kΩ baseline from that wire to column ground at the switch; other side → column ground.
expect: L3-S1 3 to column ground: LEFT 1.8 kΩ · RIGHT 10 kΩ · OFF 47 kΩ. L3-S1 6 to column ground: off 47 kΩ · hazard on about 4.27 kΩ.
caution: CK18: the 1980 tables show no OFF contact to ground on the stalks. If CK18 found none, the 47 kΩ is a fixed baseline and the ladders table is what you build to.

do: End the leg at the wiper stalk
how:
Stalk D-03: HIGH → 4.7 kΩ → the L3-S1 4 wire · LOW → 10 kΩ → L3-S1 4 · INT → 18 kΩ → L3-S1 4 · OFF → 47 kΩ → L3-S1 4.
WASH contact → the WASH sub-assembly from E7 (resistor + diode, band toward the contact) → L3-S1 4; and the same WASH terminal direct → the L3-S2 9 wire (BLU).
Common / contact returns → column ground.
expect: L3-S1 4 to column ground: HIGH 4.7 kΩ · LOW 10 kΩ · INT 18 kΩ · OFF 47 kΩ. WASH pressed: L3-S2 9 beeps to column ground.
caution: The WASH leg has a diode: an ohmmeter will not read it true. Check the resistor alone, and the diode on diode test.

do: End the leg at the horn pad and the wink plate
how:
Horn pad (steering wheel, returns to column ground through the slip ring): contact → 8.2 kΩ → the L3-S1 11 wire.
Wink plate lead, 4 wires to the plate board's header J2: pin 1 ← L3-S1 9 (BLU, wink L NC) · pin 2 ← L3-S1 10 (BLU, wink R NC) · pin 3 ← L3-S1 11 (GRY) · pin 4 → dash ground, 16 AWG BLK.
J2's housing and the plate's position are still confirm: leave this lead long, labelled, and unterminated at the plate end if the plate is not in hand.
expect: L3-S1 11 to ground: horn pressed 8.2 kΩ; with the plate fitted, wink L 18 kΩ, wink R 33 kΩ. L3-S1 9 and 10 beep to dash ground at rest and open when their wink is held.

do: End the leg at the pedal box
how:
Brake pedal switch F-11 (new, P085): contact → 4.7 kΩ → the L3-S1 5 wire; other side → dash ground.
Brake-wake plunger (P084) on the pedal: one side ← the F24 branch, other side → the L3-S1 7 wire (BLU).
Kick-down switch B-32 at the throttle pedal (kept): one terminal ← L3-S2 12 (RED); the other → L3-S3 4 (RED).
expect: L3-S1 5 to dash ground: pedal pressed 4.7 kΩ, released open. L3-S1 7 beeps to the F24 branch with the pedal pressed.

do: End the leg at the centre stack and glovebox
how:
Head unit: red (ACC) ← L3-M 1 · yellow (BATT) ← L3-M 2 · orange (ILLUM) ← L3-S1 8 · black → dash ground, 14 AWG BLK. USB-C module: + ← a branch off L3-M 1 · − → dash ground, 16 AWG BLK.
Dash illumination lamps E-06 heater panel, E-07 select lever, E-10 switch panel: RL ← the L3-S1 8 wire · B → dash ground.
Glove box lamp H-01 + ← L3-S2 10; lamp − through the lid switch H-02 → dash ground.
Parking brake switch C-04: BR ← L3-S2 11; the switch grounds through the lever bracket.
The head unit and USB-C module are fitted later: end those wires labelled and insulated.
expect: Each wire reaches the end named and is labelled there.

how:
To the dash ground star or the column ground, ring terminals (P079):
G15 · Blower motor return — L3-BLW 2 → dash ground (through the final stage · D-257) · 12 AWG BLK · x1 · 4 ft hand estimate - confirm
G16 · Head unit black → dash ground · 14 AWG BLK · x1 · 3 ft hand estimate - confirm
G17 · USB-C module − → dash ground · 16 AWG BLK · x1 · 3 ft hand estimate - confirm
G18 · Dash illumination lamps B → dash ground · 16 AWG BLK · x3 · 3 ft hand estimate - confirm
G19 · Glove box lamp switch → dash ground · 16 AWG BLK · x1 · 3 ft hand estimate - confirm
G20 · Wink switch commons → dash ground · 16 AWG BLK · x2 · 3 ft hand estimate - confirm
G21 · Brake pedal switch → dash ground · 16 AWG BLK · x1 · 3 ft hand estimate - confirm
G22 · Turn / hazard / wiper stalk returns → column ground · 16 AWG BLK · x3 · 2 ft hand estimate - confirm
G14, the bus-to-chassis lead, is the node's (E17 / E24); G36 and G42 are E38's.
expect: Every return listed has a labelled BLK wire with a ring on it.
caution: The lengths in the grounds table are hand estimates: cut each to the measured run, not to the table.

do: Test: continuity end to end, every cavity
how: Meter on the beeper. One probe on the socket in the plug cavity (use a spare pin contact as a probe tip, never a meter probe pushed into a socket), the other on the far end of that wire. Tick each cavity on the housing lists above. Through a resistor the beeper stays silent: read ohms instead.
expect: A beep for every LIVE and CAPPED cavity to its own far end, and to no other.
caution: A meter probe forced into a socket contact spreads it and the pin goes loose: probe with a mating pin.

how: Nothing plugged in at either end. Meter on its highest ohms range: each power cavity to its neighbours in the same plug, and every cavity to the ground wires of the leg.
expect: Open everywhere - the node test's mark is more than 1 MΩ (E18) - except where a resistor is fitted on purpose (the ladder and baseline resistors read their own value).
caution: Any other reading is a stray strand or a nicked wire: find it before the leg is bundled.

how:
With each switch that is already on the leg, work it through every position and read ohms at the leg-side cavity against the ladders table:
A16 key (L3-S2 2 to L3-S1 1): OFF bias only · ACC 33k · RUN 33k + 15k · START 33k + 15k + 6.8k
A15 lights (F24 branch to L3-S1 2): OFF bias only · PARK 33k · HEAD_LO 33k + 15k · HEAD_HI 33k + 15k + 8.2k · PASS 33k + 15k + 8.2k + 3.3k
A1 turn (L3-S1 3 to ground): LEFT 1.8k · RIGHT 10k · OFF 47k
A2 wiper (L3-S1 4 to ground): WASH 470 + 1N4148 · HIGH 4.7k · LOW 10k · INT 18k · OFF 47k
A8 (L3-S1 6 and 11 to ground): HAZ+HORN 4.7k ∥ 8.2k ∥ 47k · HAZARD 4.7k ∥ 47k · HORN 8.2k ∥ 47k · WINK_L 18k ∥ 47k · WINK_R 33k ∥ 47k · IDLE 47k
A3 brake only on this leg (L3-S1 5 to ground): 4.7k pressed
In the table a + on A15 / A16 means both contacts closed at once, so the resistors are in parallel.
On the leg the two A8 wires are still separate (the node splices them): L3-S1 6 alone reads 47k idle and 4.7k ∥ 47k with the hazard on; L3-S1 11 alone reads open idle, 8.2k horn, 18k wink L, 33k wink R.
A kept switch that is not on the leg yet: check its resistor sub-assembly alone here, and repeat the switch-through check at E26.
expect: Each state within 2 % of its value: 33 kΩ · 10.3 kΩ · 4.1 kΩ on the key; 33 kΩ · 10.3 kΩ · 4.6 kΩ · 1.9 kΩ on the lights; 1.8 k · 10 k · 47 k turn; 4.7 k · 10 k · 18 k · 47 k wiper; 4.27 kΩ hazard on its 47 k baseline.

how: Tug every crimp once more. Tie the bundle every 150 mm with loose ties. Do NOT final-wrap: the cabin looms are wrapped at E35 and the engine-bay looms at E33. Dust caps on every branch-end receptacle; bag the plugs so no dirt gets in the sockets.
expect: A leg that lies flat on its layout, every end labelled, nothing taped.

how:
On the board or floor, mark the dash post at one end and each node and device along the measured runs:
RT06 Dash post → Nose splice, Cowl grommet, then along the inner wing: NOT measured - confirm (the 3D model guesses 11.4 ft: planning only, never a cut length)
RT07 Nose splice → Each headlight bucket and pop-up motor, across the radiator support: NOT measured - confirm (the 3D model guesses 3.4 ft: planning only, never a cut length)
RT08 Nose splice → Front combo lamps, side markers, horns, radiator support and both inner wings: NOT measured - confirm (the 3D model guesses 6.1 ft: planning only, never a cut length)
RT09 Nose splice → Wiper motor D-02 and washer pump D-01, back along the cowl: NOT measured - confirm
RT29 Nose splice → Front bumper, radar sensor, along the bumper beam: NOT measured - confirm
A run marked NOT measured has no cut length yet: that wire waits until C1's M-2 has measured it and G13 has derived the length. Do not cut from the 3D-model guess.
The leg's pin ladder and route map are in the app's Diagrams.
expect: Every run has a measured length written beside it on the board, or is marked WAIT.
caution: A wire cut short cannot be stretched: no measured route, no cut.

how:
Cut each wire to 1.5 x its run (add the runs joined by +). Print and wrap both labels before the next wire is cut.
RUN RT06 + RT07:
  L2-P 1 Headlight LOW, both · RED 12 AWG
  L2-P 2 Headlight HIGH, both · RED 12 AWG
  L2-P 3 Pop-up motor feed (WR), both motors · RED 12 AWG
  L2-P 4 Pop-up LH down command (RY) · RED 14 AWG
  L2-S 1 Pop-up LH up command (R) · RED 14 AWG
  L2-S 2 Pop-up RH up command (R) · RED 14 AWG
  L2-S 6 Pop-up RH down command (RY) · RED 14 AWG
RUN RT06 + RT08:
  L2-M 3 Horns, both · ORN 14 AWG
  L2-M 5 Turn LEFT front · RED 16 AWG
  L2-M 6 Turn RIGHT front · RED 16 AWG
  L2-M 7 Park + side markers, front · ORN 14 AWG
  L2-S 5 Outside-air temperature sensor · GRY 16 AWG
RUN RT06 + RT09:
  L2-M 1 Wiper LOW brush · ORN 14 AWG
  L2-M 2 Wiper HIGH brush · ORN 14 AWG
  L2-M 4 Washer pump feed · ORN 14 AWG
  L2-M 8 Wiper park feed — future motor family · RED 16 AWG
  L2-S 3 Wiper park sense · GRY 16 AWG
  L2-S 4 Wiper park return — future motor family · GRY 16 AWG
RUN RT06 + RT29:
  L2-R 1 Radar front sensor A · GRY 16 AWG
  L2-R 2 Radar front sensor B · GRY 16 AWG
  L2-R 3 Radar front sensor C · GRY 16 AWG
The nose splices fan out: the trunk wire is cut to RT06, each branch to its own run from the nose splice.
L2-OAT 1 is the far end of the L2-S 5 wire; L2-RDR 1-3 are the far ends of L2-R 1-3.
expect: One labelled wire per line of the list, laid along its run on the board.

how:
L2-P is a DTP06-4S, the 4-way plug (kit P131): size-12 socket contacts (P026); wedgelock WP-4S.
1 · Headlight LOW, both · RED 12 AWG → Splice at the nose → 14 AWG branch to each lamp plug, terminal RY
2 · Headlight HIGH, both · RED 12 AWG → Splice at the nose → 14 AWG branch to each lamp plug, terminal RL
3 · Pop-up motor feed (WR), both motors · RED 12 AWG → Splice at the nose → 12 AWG branch to motor E-03 terminal WR and motor E-04 terminal WR, as the headlights on L2-P 1 / 2 (D-487; one feed per motor until then) - each …
4 · Pop-up LH down command (RY) · RED 14 AWG → Motor E-03 terminal RY - the down command into the motor's own relay (SP-584, D-460); N14 at the node. A command, not the motor current, but behind O1's 25 A soft fuse, …
Each wire: strip, crimp the socket in the 4-indent crimper, push in from the wire side until it clicks, tug. Work in cavity order. Then the sealing plugs, then the wedgelock.
expect: Every contact clicked and tugged; no cavity left empty; the wedgelock snaps in flush; the code L2-P is on the shell.
caution: Do not pin cavities 3 and 4 until CK08 is read.

how:
L2-M is a DT06-8S, the 8-way plug (kit P101): size-16 socket contacts: P022 for 16-18 AWG, P024 for 14 AWG; wedgelock W8S.
1 · Wiper LOW brush · ORN 14 AWG → Wiper motor D-02, terminal LW
2 · Wiper HIGH brush · ORN 14 AWG → Wiper motor D-02, terminal LR
3 · Horns, both · ORN 14 AWG → Splice at the nose → each horn's terminal GY
4 · Washer pump feed · ORN 14 AWG → Washer motor D-01, terminal LB
5 · Turn LEFT front · RED 16 AWG → Front combo lamp F-05, terminal GR
6 · Turn RIGHT front · RED 16 AWG → Front combo lamp F-06, terminal GO
7 · Park + side markers, front · ORN 14 AWG → Splice at the nose → F-05 RG, F-06 RG, F-12 RG, F-13 RG
8 · Wiper park feed — future motor family · RED 16 AWG · CAPPED → Held as the fused park feed a self-parking motor needs; block A position F13 is its protection when it is taken up (D-317)
Each wire: strip, crimp the socket in the 4-indent crimper, push in from the wire side until it clicks, tug. Work in cavity order. Then the sealing plugs, then the wedgelock.
expect: Every contact clicked and tugged; no cavity left empty; the wedgelock snaps in flush; the code L2-M is on the shell.

how:
L2-S is a DT06-6S, the 6-way plug (kit P099): size-16 socket contacts: P022 for 16-18 AWG, P024 for 14 AWG; wedgelock W6S.
1 · Pop-up LH up command (R) · RED 14 AWG → Motor E-03 terminal R - the up command into the motor's own relay (SP-584, D-460); N12 at the node; 14 AWG behind O1's 25 A soft fuse (D-487). Was A4's transit contact …
2 · Pop-up RH up command (R) · RED 14 AWG → Motor E-04 terminal R - the up command (SP-584, D-460); N13 at the node; 14 AWG (D-487). Was A5's transit contact: YG is capped at the motor
3 · Wiper park sense · GRY 16 AWG → 47 kΩ baseline to the front star ground at the L2-S plug, as A4/A5 (D-368) - covers the run to the park contact; a break in the brake branch reads as brake never …
4 · Wiper park return — future motor family · GRY 16 AWG · CAPPED → Run to the wiper branch and left unpinned there: a DIN 72552 motor's park return is pinned into this cavity at the branch, no leg re-run (D-317)
5 · Outside-air temperature sensor · GRY 16 AWG · CAPPED → L2-OAT 1 — the outside-air sensor receptacle ahead of the radiator, dust-capped; the thermistor's other lead grounds at the front star (D-256 → D-329, D-274)
6 · Pop-up RH down command (RY) · RED 14 AWG → Motor E-04 terminal RY - the down command (SP-584, D-460); N15 at the node; 14 AWG (D-487). Was a sealing plug since D-329
Cavity 3: before the contact goes in, join a 47 kΩ (E7 sub-assembly) onto the GRY wire right behind the plug; its other lead goes on 16 AWG BLK to a ring for the front star.
Cavity 4: the wire is pinned here at the plug, run to the wiper branch, and left cut, labelled and capped there.
Each wire: strip, crimp the socket in the 4-indent crimper, push in from the wire side until it clicks, tug. Work in cavity order. Then the sealing plugs, then the wedgelock.
expect: Every contact clicked and tugged; no cavity left empty; the wedgelock snaps in flush; the code L2-S is on the shell.
caution: Do not pin cavities 1, 2 and 6 until CK08 is read.

how:
L2-R is a DT06-4S, the 4-way plug (kit P124): size-16 socket contacts: P022 for 16-18 AWG, P024 for 14 AWG; wedgelock W4S.
1 · Radar front sensor A · GRY 16 AWG · CAPPED → L2-RDR 1 at the nose, dust-capped (A16)
2 · Radar front sensor B · GRY 16 AWG · CAPPED → L2-RDR 2 at the nose, dust-capped (A16)
3 · Radar front sensor C · GRY 16 AWG · CAPPED → L2-RDR 3 at the nose, dust-capped (A16)
4 · sealing plug, size 16
Each wire: strip, crimp the socket in the 4-indent crimper, push in from the wire side until it clicks, tug. Work in cavity order. Then the sealing plugs, then the wedgelock.
expect: Every contact clicked and tugged; 1 sealing plug fitted; the wedgelock snaps in flush; the code L2-R is on the shell.

how:
Sealed crimp butt splices with adhesive heat-shrink (P078), staggered so the bundle does not swell in one place:
L2-P 1 (12 AWG) → a 14 AWG branch to each headlamp plug, terminal RY
L2-P 2 (12 AWG) → a 14 AWG branch to each headlamp plug, terminal RL
L2-P 3 (12 AWG) → a 12 AWG branch to motor E-03 terminal WR and to motor E-04 terminal WR
L2-M 3 (14 AWG) → each horn's terminal GY
L2-M 7 (14 AWG) → F-05 RG, F-06 RG, F-12 RG, F-13 RG
expect: Each splice survives a firm tug; glue shows at both ends of the shrink.
caution: The splice kit has three sizes (22-18, 16-14, 12-10); the record does not say which takes a trunk and two branches: make one on scrap and tug it first.

do: End the leg at the pop-up motors
how:
Motor E-03 (left): WR ← the L2-P 3 branch · R (up) ← L2-S 1 · RY (down) ← L2-P 4 · YG capped at the motor.
Motor E-04 (right): WR ← the L2-P 3 branch · R (up) ← L2-S 2 · RY (down) ← L2-S 6 · YG capped.
Each bucket: a 14 AWG BLK strap to the front star (G07).
The motors keep their factory plugs (E-03 / E-04 connectors).
expect: Each wire labelled with its motor terminal letter.
caution: YG is +12 V while the motor runs: cap it sealed, never ground it.

do: End the leg at the headlamps
how: Each lamp E-08 (left), E-09 (right): RY ← its L2-P 1 branch · RL ← its L2-P 2 branch · B → front star, 14 AWG BLK (G06).
expect: Two lamps, three wires each.

do: End the leg at the wiper motor and washer pump
how:
Wiper motor D-02: LW ← L2-M 1 · LR ← L2-M 2 · L → 12 kΩ → L2-S 3 · LB capped, unconnected · B → front star, 14 AWG BLK (G11).
The L2-S 4 and L2-M 8 wires end here, cut, labelled CAPPED and sealed.
Washer pump D-01: LB (+) ← L2-M 4 · LY (−) → front star, 16 AWG BLK (G12).
expect: L2-S 3 reads 12 kΩ to the motor L end.
caution: CK09 may have changed which terminal is the park output: build to the cavity rows as they stand after CK09.

do: End the leg at the front lamps and horns
how:
Front combo F-05 (left): GR ← L2-M 5 · RG ← the L2-M 7 splice · B → front star, 16 AWG BLK (G08). F-06 (right): GO ← L2-M 6 · RG · B.
Side markers F-12 (left), F-13 (right): RG ← the L2-M 7 splice · B → front star (G09).
Horns F-09, F-10: GY ← the L2-M 3 splice; a 14 AWG BLK ring under each horn's mounting bolt → front star (G10).
expect: Each lamp and horn has its feed and its own ground wire.

do: Fit the branch-end receptacles L2-OAT and L2-RDR
how:

do: Test: continuity end to end, every cavity
how: Meter on the beeper. One probe on the socket in the plug cavity (use a spare pin contact as a probe tip, never a meter probe pushed into a socket), the other on the far end of that wire. Tick each cavity on the housing lists above. Through a resistor the beeper stays silent: read ohms instead.
expect: A beep for every LIVE and CAPPED cavity to its own far end, and to no other.
caution: A meter probe forced into a socket contact spreads it and the pin goes loose: probe with a mating pin.

how: Nothing plugged in at either end. Meter on its highest ohms range: each power cavity to its neighbours in the same plug, and every cavity to the ground wires of the leg.
expect: Open everywhere - the node test's mark is more than 1 MΩ (E18) - except where a resistor is fitted on purpose (the ladder and baseline resistors read their own value).
caution: Any other reading is a stray strand or a nicked wire: find it before the leg is bundled.

how:
L2-S 3 to its front-star ring: BRAKE+PARKED 4.7k ∥ 12k ∥ 47k · BRAKE 4.7k ∥ 47k · PARKED 12k ∥ 47k · IDLE 47k.
On this leg alone, with the wiper parked or not connected, cavity 3 shows the 47 kΩ baseline; through the park contact it shows 12 kΩ in parallel with it.
expect: 47 kΩ at rest; about 9.6 kΩ with the park contact closed to ground.

how: Tug every crimp once more. Tie the bundle every 150 mm with loose ties. Do NOT final-wrap: the cabin looms are wrapped at E35 and the engine-bay looms at E33. Dust caps on every branch-end receptacle; bag the plugs so no dirt gets in the sockets.

how: Tug every crimp once more. Tie the bundle every 150 mm with loose ties. Do NOT final-wrap: the cabin looms are wrapped at E35 and the engine-bay looms at E33. Dust caps on every branch-end receptacle; bag the plugs so no dirt gets in the sockets.
expect: A leg that lies flat on its layout, every end labelled, nothing taped.

how:
On the board or floor, mark the dash post at one end and each node and device along the measured runs:
RT01 Dash post → Engine-bay junction, Firewall grommet, passenger side: NOT measured - confirm
RT02 Engine-bay junction → Coils and igniters B-18 to B-21, along the upper rear housing: NOT measured - confirm
RT03 Engine-bay junction → Alternator A-08, down the front of the block: NOT measured - confirm
RT04 Engine-bay junction → Water temp C-02 and oil pressure C-09, rear housing, gauge ports: NOT measured - confirm
RT05 Engine-bay junction → Starter, K9 and the inhibitor A-06, under the intake: NOT measured - confirm
RT26 Engine-bay junction → Master cylinder, brake-fluid switch, along the firewall to the reservoir: NOT measured - confirm
A run marked NOT measured has no cut length yet: that wire waits until C1's M-2 has measured it and G13 has derived the length. Do not cut from the 3D-model guess.
The leg's pin ladder and route map are in the app's Diagrams.
expect: Every run has a measured length written beside it on the board, or is marked WAIT.
caution: A wire cut short cannot be stretched: no measured route, no cut.

how:
Cut each wire to 1.5 x its run (add the runs joined by +). Print and wrap both labels before the next wire is cut.
RUN RT01 + RT02:
  L1-P 1 Ignition feed — coils and igniters · RED 12 AWG
  L1-S1 6 Tachometer pulse — SHIELDED · shielded cable, 16 AWG core (P074)
RUN RT01 + RT03:
  L1-S1 2 Alternator excitation (field feed) · RED 16 AWG
  L1-S2 8 Alternator charge-lamp sense · GRY 16 AWG
RUN RT01 + RT04:
  L1-S1 3 Water temperature sender · GRY 16 AWG
  L1-S1 4 Oil pressure sender · GRY 16 AWG
RUN RT01 + RT05:
  L1-S1 1 Start relay K9 coil · RED 16 AWG
  L1-S1 11 Inhibitor switch — P/N contact (crank interlock) · GRY 16 AWG
  L1-S2 7 Inhibitor switch — R contact (reverse lamps) · GRY 16 AWG
RUN RT01 + RT26:
  L1-S2 1 Brake fluid level switch · GRY 16 AWG
K9's two 10 AWG RED contact wires (F17 → K9 30, K9 87 → starter S) are cables C08 / C09: their lengths are hand estimates - cut to the measured run along RT05.
expect: One labelled wire per line of the list, laid along its run on the board.

how:
L1-P is a DTP06-4S, the 4-way plug (kit P131): size-12 socket contacts (P026); wedgelock WP-4S.
1 · Ignition feed — coils and igniters · RED 12 AWG → Splice at the coil bracket → BW of coil T, coil L, igniter T, igniter L
2 · sealing plug, size 12, in this plug - RESERVED: LS swap reserve — ECU + injectors is pinned on the receptacle only
3 · sealing plug, size 12, in this plug - RESERVED: LS swap reserve — cooling fan is pinned on the receptacle only
4 · sealing plug, size 12
Each wire: strip, crimp the socket in the 4-indent crimper, push in from the wire side until it clicks, tug. Work in cavity order. Then the sealing plugs, then the wedgelock.
expect: Every contact clicked and tugged; 3 sealing plugs fitted; the wedgelock snaps in flush; the code L1-P is on the shell.
caution: Cavities 2, 3 and 4 take size-12 sealing plugs (P029), not the size-16 ones.

how:
L1-S1 is a DT06-12S, the 12-way plug (kit P115): size-16 socket contacts: P022 for 16-18 AWG, P024 for 14 AWG; wedgelock W12S.
1 · Start relay K9 coil · RED 16 AWG → K9 terminal 86 (inner fender)
2 · Alternator excitation (field feed) · RED 16 AWG → Alternator plug A-08, terminal BW
3 · Water temperature sender · GRY 16 AWG → Sender C-02, spade — factory wire YW
4 · Oil pressure sender · GRY 16 AWG → Sender C-09, spade — factory wire BrY
5 · sealing plug, size 16
6 · Tachometer pulse — SHIELDED · shielded cable, 16 AWG core (P074) → Coil T (B-18) negative terminal — factory wire YG. Shield grounded at the dash node end only (N48, colours): the engine end of the shield is cut back and insulated, so …
7 · sealing plug, size 16
8 · sealing plug, size 16
9 · sealing plug, size 16
10 · sealing plug, size 16
11 · Inhibitor switch — P/N contact (crank interlock) · GRY 16 AWG → Inhibitor A-06: 8.2 kΩ in the lead to terminal BY; terminal BW → block ground. The 47 kΩ baseline from this lead to the block ground at the switch (D-487: it sat at the …
12 · sealing plug, size 16
Cavity 6 is the shielded cable's core: strip the jacket back, fold the drain and shield back out of the way, crimp the core only.
How the drain is bonded at this plug is not in the record: leave 150 mm of drain here, insulated, and raise a note before trimming it.
Each wire: strip, crimp the socket in the 4-indent crimper, push in from the wire side until it clicks, tug. Work in cavity order. Then the sealing plugs, then the wedgelock.
expect: Every contact clicked and tugged; 6 sealing plugs fitted; the wedgelock snaps in flush; the code L1-S1 is on the shell.
caution: A shield strand in the crimp shorts the tach to ground.

how:
L1-S2 is a DT06-12S, the 12-way plug (kit P115): size-16 socket contacts: P022 for 16-18 AWG, P024 for 14 AWG; wedgelock W12S.
1 · Brake fluid level switch · GRY 16 AWG → Reservoir switch C-05: terminal BR; terminal B → block ground
2 · sealing plug, size 16
3 · sealing plug, size 16
4 · sealing plug, size 16
5 · sealing plug, size 16
6 · sealing plug, size 16
7 · Inhibitor switch — R contact (reverse lamps) · GRY 16 AWG → Inhibitor A-06: 8.2 kΩ in the lead to terminal GY; terminal RW → block ground. The 47 kΩ baseline from this lead to the block ground at the switch (D-487)
8 · Alternator charge-lamp sense · GRY 16 AWG → Alternator plug A-08, terminal WB
9 · sealing plug, size 16, in this plug - RESERVED: Phase-2 sensor supply — +12 V switched is pinned on the receptacle only
10 · sealing plug, size 16
11 · sealing plug, size 16, in this plug - RESERVED: Phase-2 sensor signal spare is pinned on the receptacle only
12 · sealing plug, size 16
Each wire: strip, crimp the socket in the 4-indent crimper, push in from the wire side until it clicks, tug. Work in cavity order. Then the sealing plugs, then the wedgelock.
expect: Every contact clicked and tugged; 9 sealing plugs fitted; the wedgelock snaps in flush; the code L1-S2 is on the shell.

how:
L1-P 1 (12 AWG RED trunk) → a sealed splice at the coil bracket → 14 AWG branches to terminal BW of coil T (B-18), coil L (B-19), igniter T (B-20) and igniter L (B-21).
The suppression capacitor (P135): its lead on the same splice, its ring-lug case under a bracket bolt.
The YL (leading pulse) wire is not used.
expect: L1-P 1 beeps to all four BW ends and to the capacitor lead.
caution: This is the ignition feed: every joint here is a sealed crimp, tugged.

do: End the tach cable at the coil
how:
Core → coil T (B-18) negative terminal, factory wire YG.
At this end cut the shield and drain back and seal the end with adhesive heat-shrink so no strand shows.
Lay the cable so it crosses the coil and igniter leads at 90 degrees and is never within 50 mm parallel to one.
expect: Core to shield reads open; the core beeps end to end.

how:
Weatherproof 5-pin socket (P005):
86 ← L1-S1 1 (16 AWG RED)
85 → block ground, 16 AWG BLK (G02)
30 ← F17, 10 AWG RED (from the MIDI holder at the starter B+ stud)
87 → the starter S terminal (factory wire BW), 10 AWG RED
Confirm the socket's terminals accept 10 AWG before crimping.
expect: Four wires in the socket, each tugged; the relay (P004) clicks into it.
caution: The 30 wire is live from the battery whenever the master disconnect is closed: its far end stays insulated until E27.

do: End the leg at the alternator and the senders
how:
Alternator plug A-08: BW ← L1-S1 2 (RED) · WB ← L1-S2 8 (GRY).
Water-temp sender C-02: spade ← L1-S1 3 (GRY). Oil-pressure sender C-09: spade ← L1-S1 4 (GRY). Both ground through their threads.
Brake-fluid switch C-05: BR ← L1-S2 1 (GRY) · B → block ground, 16 AWG BLK (G04).
expect: Each wire labelled with its device and terminal.

do: End the leg at the inhibitor switch
how:
Switch A-06, 4-pin, on the transmission:
BY ← 8.2 kΩ ← L1-S1 11 (GRY) · BW → block ground, 16 AWG BLK
GY ← 8.2 kΩ ← L1-S2 7 (GRY) · RW → block ground, 16 AWG BLK
A 47 kΩ baseline from each GRY lead to the block ground wire, at the switch.
Resistors are the E7 sub-assemblies, soldered and heat-shrunk.
expect: Each GRY lead reads 47 kΩ to its ground wire with the contact open.

how:
To the engine block, ring terminals (P079):
G02 · K9 85 → block · 16 AWG BLK · x1 · 3 ft hand estimate - confirm
G03 · Inhibitor BW and RW → block · 16 AWG BLK · x2 · 3 ft hand estimate - confirm
G04 · Brake fluid switch B → block · 16 AWG BLK · x1 · 3 ft hand estimate - confirm
G39 is the swap's fan return: not this build.
expect: Every return has a labelled BLK wire with a ring.
caution: Lengths in the table are hand estimates: cut to the measured run.

do: Test: continuity end to end, every cavity
how: Meter on the beeper. One probe on the socket in the plug cavity (use a spare pin contact as a probe tip, never a meter probe pushed into a socket), the other on the far end of that wire. Tick each cavity on the housing lists above. Through a resistor the beeper stays silent: read ohms instead.
expect: A beep for every LIVE and CAPPED cavity to its own far end, and to no other. Tach core: open to its shield.
caution: A meter probe forced into a socket contact spreads it and the pin goes loose: probe with a mating pin.

how: Nothing plugged in at either end. Meter on its highest ohms range: each power cavity to its neighbours in the same plug, and every cavity to the ground wires of the leg.
expect: Open everywhere - the node test's mark is more than 1 MΩ (E18) - except where a resistor is fitted on purpose (the ladder and baseline resistors read their own value).
caution: Any other reading is a stray strand or a nicked wire: find it before the leg is bundled.

how:
L1-S1 11 to its block-ground wire: CRANK_OK 8.2k ∥ 47k · IDLE 47k.
L1-S2 7 to its block-ground wire: REVERSE 8.2k ∥ 47k · IDLE 47k.
With the switch on the leg, move the lever through P, R, N.
expect: 47 kΩ idle; about 6.98 kΩ with the contact closed (8.2 kΩ in parallel with 47 kΩ).

how: Tug every crimp once more. Tie the bundle every 150 mm with loose ties. Do NOT final-wrap: the cabin looms are wrapped at E35 and the engine-bay looms at E33. Dust caps on every branch-end receptacle; bag the plugs so no dirt gets in the sockets.
expect: A leg that lies flat on its layout, every end labelled, nothing taped.

do: Check what arrived against the BOM
how: The ICU carrier BOM csv, line by line, against the bags. Boards: look at both sides for scratches and check the outline against the DT13 receptacles.
expect: Every line present.

how: In a terminal on the Mac: go to the tests folder inside the electrical design folder (02-PROJECTS/01-electrical/00-design/tests) and run ./run.sh. It runs every host suite, checks the board sheets against the record and compiles every sketch for its target.
expect: Exit code 0, every suite green.
caution: Never flash a Teensy on a red suite.

do: Solder the board, power parts first
how:
Input protection and the 5 V buck first (the SS34 diodes, the SMBJ33A, the buck and its inductor and capacitors), then stop and test (next step).
Then the small parts by height: resistors, capacitors, the BAT54S clamps, the CAN transceiver, the FETs.
Then the sockets and headers: the Teensy socket, the XIAO and IMU sockets, the display header, the two DT13 receptacles last.
R18 has no value yet: leave it out until a bench result picks one of the three bought.
expect: Every joint wetted; no bridges under the magnifier.
caution: The buck is a 2 x 3 mm leadless package: it needs hot air or a hot plate, and its orientation mark matched to the board.

do: Power the bare board, no Teensy
how:
Bench supply at 12 V with its current limit set low (a few hundred mA - a bench setting, not a record figure). + to DP-ICU-A 1, − to DP-ICU-A 3.
Measure at the Teensy socket's VIN pad.
expect: 5 V on VIN; the supply shows a few mA, not the limit.
caution: If the supply hits its limit, switch off at once: something is bridged or reversed.

do: Fit the PSRAM and socket the Teensy
how: Solder the two 8 MB PSRAM chips (P108) to the pads under the Teensy 4.1, then press the Teensy into its socket with the USB end where the board marks pad 1.
expect: Teensy seated square, USB end at the marked end.
caution: A Teensy in backwards puts 5 V on a ground pin.

how:
Arduino IDE (Teensyduino) on the Mac: Board Teensy 4.1, CPU 600 MHz, library ACAN_T4 (not FlexCAN_T4). Open the sketch, plug the Teensy in by USB, Upload.
The sketch is icu.ino in the display unit's firmware folder. Do not put the simulator sources in the sketch folder.
expect: The serial monitor prints the firmware version at boot.

how: The icu_radio sketch for the XIAO ESP32C3, over its own USB. Then seat the XIAO in its socket.
expect: It uploads; the ICU later reports battery data from it.
caution: Never write to the BMS and never touch its FFE7 or DFU service.

how:
A second Teensy running pmu_sim and a third running tach_simulator (P142).
pmu_sim needs an SN65HVD230 module (P143) with its headers soldered; the carrier has its own transceiver.
One twisted pair between them: CAN H to DP-ICU-A 4, CAN L to DP-ICU-A 5, with a 120 Ω resistor (P070) across the pair at each end.
expect: The ICU's diagnostics page shows frames arriving.

how: Six signal wires from the carrier's display header to the eval board: CS 10, MOSI 11, MISO 12, SCK 13, PD 9, INT 24, plus power and ground as the eval board's sheet shows.
expect: The eval board's screen lights and draws the DRIVE page.
caution: The eval board's own supply pins are on its datasheet, not in the record: read it before applying power.

how:
A potentiometer from DP-ICU-B 1, then 2, then 3 to ground stands in for the water-temp, oil-pressure and fuel senders.
tach_simulator's pulse output into DP-ICU-B 4.
12 V onto DP-ICU-B 10, 11 and 12 in turn for the left turn, right turn and high-beam tell-tales.
DP-ICU-B 6 to ground for the brake warning.
12 V on DP-ICU-A 2 for the illumination reference.
expect: Each gauge follows its input; each tell-tale lights with its line; BRAKE shows with cavity 6 low; the brightness of the display follows the voltage on cavity 2, its dimming reference.

how: Unplug the PMU simulator's power.
expect: Volts blanks; rpm, temperature, pressure and fuel carry on.
caution: If everything blanks, stop and raise a note: the gauges must not depend on the bus.

how: 12 V through a 5 A fuse onto DP-ICU-A 6. Watch the backlight output switch with the firmware.
expect: Backlight on with the unit awake, off when it is told off.

do: Bring up the real bar panel
how:
Only after M-1 has sized the aperture and the panel (P118) and its bridge (P119) are in hand.
Connect chain (ii) and run the timing check V-084: pixel clock and sync polarity against the panel.
expect: A stable full-width picture, no tearing or rolling.
caution: Until then the eval board is the display: do not buy the glass early.

how: Run tach_simulator's speed channel into DP-ICU-B 8 until the odometer moves. Note the figure. Power off, wait, power on. Then check the card (P151) holds it too.
expect: The same odometer figure after the power cycle, and on the card.

do: Zero the IMU and check the battery path
how: Board flat and still: zero the IMU. With the battery in range: the four cell counts summed agree with the advertised pack millivolts.
expect: IMU reads zero at rest; cells sum to the pack figure.

how: Note the version and what was proved in the app.
expect: A note the agent can turn into a bring-up log row.

how: H-002 is done in the app and the agent reports the board redrawn to V-102's measurement with its design-rule check at zero (CK26).
expect: A final board, not the provisional outline.

how: Ask the agent for the final packages: the DCU carrier, the panel board and the upper connector board - each a gerbers zip and a BOM csv.
expect: Three zips and three BOMs.

how: Upload each zip: 2 layers, 1.6 mm, 1 oz copper, the smallest batch. Check each reported outline against the board's size.
expect: Three boards in one order, previews matching the board pictures.

how:
From each BOM csv, only what the bench order did not leave in hand.
The lines: transceivers (P145), the two bucks (P146), protection (P147), Teensy socket headers (P148), the comfort stage (P149), the DT13 receptacles (P150, P153, P194), the ribbon and its headers (P157), the inductor (P177), the small headers (P178), the ribbon-line parts (P193), the panel's keys, encoders, lights and driver (P155, P173, P192), the inside leads (P196).
Check every line the BOM marks confirm on the distributor's page; check Q3's voltage rating.
expect: An order whose lines tick off against the BOMs.

do: Solder the carrier, power parts first
how:
Input protection and the logic buck first, then stop and test (next step).
Then the small parts by height, the power switches and the bridge driver, then sockets, headers and the DT13 receptacles last.
Leave out every part the BOM marks not fitted.
expect: Every joint wetted; no bridges under the magnifier.
caution: The power switches have exposed pads underneath: they need hot air or a hot plate.

do: Power the bare board, no Teensy
how:
Bench supply 12 V with its current limit set low (a few hundred mA - a bench setting): + to DP-DCU 1, − to DP-DCU 3.
Measure the Teensy socket's VIN pad.
expect: 5 V on VIN; a few mA from the supply.
caution: Switch off at once if the supply hits its limit.

how: 12 V, the same low limit, + to DP-DCU-C 5 and − to DP-DCU-C 6. Measure the +5 V pin of a servo header.
expect: 5 V on the servo rail.

do: Socket the Teensy and note it
how: Press a Teensy 4.1 (P142) into its socket, USB end at the marked end. Note in the app that the board is built.
expect: Ready for F6.

how: In a terminal on the Mac: go to the tests folder inside the electrical design folder (02-PROJECTS/01-electrical/00-design/tests) and run ./run.sh. It runs every host suite, checks the board sheets against the record and compiles every sketch for its target.
expect: Exit code 0.
caution: Never flash on a red suite.

how:
Arduino IDE (Teensyduino) on the Mac: Board Teensy 4.1, CPU 600 MHz, library ACAN_T4 (not FlexCAN_T4). Open the sketch, plug the Teensy in by USB, Upload.
The sketch is dcu.ino in the control unit's firmware folder.
expect: The serial monitor prints the DCU firmware version at boot.

do: Connect power and the bench bus
how:
Bench supply 12 V: + through a 3 A fuse (F22's rating) to DP-DCU 1, − to DP-DCU 3.
The PMU simulator Teensy with its transceiver: CAN H to DP-DCU 4, CAN L to DP-DCU 5, 120 Ω (P070) across the pair at each end.
The panel board on its 26-way ribbon; the upper connector board on its inside leads.
expect: The DCU boots; frames show on the simulator.

do: Prove every output is off at reset
how:
A lamp from each of DP-DCU-B 1, 2, 3, 4, 9 and DP-DCU 6 to ground; a lamp from +12 V to each of DP-DCU-C 1, 2, 3, 4 and DP-DCU-B 10, 11.
12 V to DP-DCU-C 5, ground to DP-DCU-C 6, 7, 8.
Power up; power-cycle three times; then upload the firmware once more with the lamps connected, which restarts the Teensy.
expect: No lamp lights or flickers at any moment.
caution: Any flicker is a fault to fix before this unit goes near the car.

how: Press each panel key in turn: fan mode, recirculate, rear defog, mirror defog, the two window switches up and down, and the left plate's hatch and fuel-door keys if the plate is connected (DP-DCU-E).
expect: Each press and release registers once, on its own key.

do: Read the encoders and the thumbstick
how: Turn the centre knob and press it; turn each seat knob. Move the mirror stick in both axes and press it. Set the stick's centre and dead-band.
expect: Each click counts once in the right direction; the stick rests at centre and reads both ways on both axes.

how: Hold each window switch: watch the lamp on DP-DCU-B 1, 2, 3, 4 in turn. Try up and down of one side together.
expect: One lamp per command; never both lamps of one side at once.

how:
A relay coil from +12 V to DP-DCU-B 10, then 11. Set the PMU simulator's key to OFF. Press the hatch key, then the fuel-door key.
Then set the key to ON and press again.
expect: Key OFF: the relay clicks and drops out again after about 1.5 s, key held or not. Key ON: nothing - the release is refused.
caution: Never both selects at once.

how: Lamps between DP-DCU-B 5 and 6 (left motor) and 5 and 7 (right motor), and from +12 V to 8 (clutch). Move the stick each way, then press to change sides.
expect: A lamp follows the stick on the selected side only.

how:
Turn each seat knob to heat, then to cool: lamps on DP-DCU-C 1-4.
Press the rear defog key, then the mirror-defog key: note which lights the mirror-heat lamp on DP-DCU-B 9 (the channel row says mirror heat follows the defogger, D-442; the panel has had its own mirror-defog key since D-492).
Zero the comfort current reading with everything off, then check it with one known load.
expect: Heat and cool of one seat never light together; the mirror-heat lamp lights from a defog key; the current reading is zero at no load.

how: Let the unit go to sleep, then press a panel key. Lamp or meter on DP-DCU 6.
expect: DP-DCU 6 goes to about 12 V on the press.

do: Check blower duty, servos and temperatures
how:
Meter or scope on DP-DCU-D 6 against 7: duty follows the fan setting and is zero through a reset.
With a servo in hand on DP-DCU-D 1, 4, 5: it moves to each end; set the endpoints. One servo at a time.
A 10 kΩ NTC (P154) on DP-DCU-D 8 / 9 and one on DP-DCU 2 to ground: compare with the thermometer.
expect: Duty 0-100 %; the servo holds each end without buzzing; both temperatures within a degree or two of the thermometer - confirm.

how: Meter in series in the DP-DCU 1 feed, 10 A range first then mA, unit asleep.
expect: About 10 mA - confirm; write down what it is.

how: Note the version, the sleeping current and any fault in the app.
expect: A note the agent can turn into a bring-up log row. E26 plugs the unit into the car.

do: Lay out the parts and zero the calipers
how: Close the jaws, zero, and check on something known (a drill shank). One part at a time on a white sheet; photograph each reading with the calipers in shot.
expect: Calipers read 0.00 closed.

how:
Pin pitch along the row and between rows (expect 4.445 and 6.35 mm).
Pin diameter (for the hole size).
Flange face to the centre of the pin field (expect 18.675 mm).
The three flange holes: positions and diameter. On the 12-way, confirm the centre hole exists.
How far the housing stands off the board, and which corner cavity 1 is (read the moulded number).
On the 6-way: the housing's offset from its pin field (TE's model shows 1.54 mm).
expect: Each within 0.2 mm of the figure, or written down as found.

do: Measure the Teensy 4.1 on its headers (P142, P110)
how:
Row-to-row spacing (expect 15.24 mm).
Height of the Teensy's underside above the carrier when seated in the female headers - the PSRAM chips go under there.
Which pads the socket reaches: is VBAT one of them?
expect: Row spacing within 0.2 mm; a clearance figure in mm; VBAT yes or no.

do: Measure the XIAO ESP32C3 (P116) and the IMU breakout (P109)
how:
XIAO: castellation row spacing (expect 15.24 mm), board outline, and how far the u.FL antenna connector overhangs.
IMU breakout: the two header rows (one of 6, one of 5 holes), their spacing and the outline.
expect: Readings written down.

do: Measure the BT817 eval board's header (P117)
how: The header the carrier's display header J4 mates (CN8 on the ME817EV): pitch, pin count, keying, and its position on the eval board.
expect: Readings written down.

do: Hold the outline against the binnacle space
how: From C4's numbers: the 110 x 80 mm outline, plus the enclosure wall and the mated plugs, inside the measured length, width and depth.
expect: It fits with room for the wall and the plugs, or the note says by how much it does not.

do: Enter the readings and hand over
how: Every reading as a note in the app. The agent then corrects the footprints and models, re-runs the design-rule check to zero, re-exports the 3D model of each board and re-runs the enclosure fit check.
expect: The agent's report: design-rule check zero, enclosure fit check clear.

how: F11 ticked with the agent's clean report; F1's printed enclosure closed around a bare board (CK27).
expect: Both done.
caution: Ordering before the fit test risks a second re-spin.

how: Ask the agent (a plan run) for the final ICU carrier fab package: the gerbers zip and the BOM csv, exported after F11's changes.
expect: A zip and a BOM whose revision is later than rev A.

how: At the board house: upload the zip. 2 layers, 1.6 mm, 1 oz copper, quantity the smallest batch (five). Check the outline size it reports against the board's size after F11.
expect: The preview shows the board's shape with the two DT13 footprints on one edge.

do: Check the BOM for parts not already in hand
how: Against what Y18 bought for the bench revision: order only what the final board changed or used up. Every line marked confirm in the BOM is checked on the distributor's page before buying.
expect: A short list, or nothing.

how: Pay. Note the order number, count and price in the app.
expect: Order confirmed.

do: Check the two rows before it are ticked
how: In the app: A1 (cart gaps) and A6 (cable listings) both done, and the blocks list shows nothing open that changes a cart line.
expect: A0 shows as ready.
