how: P068 Barrier terminal strip, 8 position, 12 V rated: 2 · P069 Metal-film resistor kit, E24 1 %, 1/4 W: 1 · P070 120 Ω 1 % 1/4 W resistors: 10 · P071 Schottky diode 1N5819: 22 · P072 NPN transistor 2N3904: 10 · P073 Inline ATC fuse holder, 2-pack: 1 · P074 Shielded cable, 16–18 AWG single core with drain, 15...: 1 · P114 100 Ω 1 W 1 % metal-film resistor: 2 · P116 ESP32-C3 module ×2: 2 · P134 Perfboard 5 × 7 cm, 2-pack, with M3 standoffs: 1 set · P135 Ignition noise-suppression capacitor, automotive,...: 2 · P138 USB-to-CAN interface cable, Ecumaster / PCAN / Kvaser...: 1 · P139 Limp-home glovebox kit - three fused jumpers (10 A,...: 1 set · P158 Film capacitor 2.2 µF, 50 V or higher: 5 (target 2).
expect: Every row matches.

do: Count the Amazon consumables and the rest
how: P075 Label tape: 3 (target 4) · P076 Clear heat-shrink 3/16 in, 2:1: 3 · P077 Adhesive-lined heat-shrink assortment 3:1, incl....: 1 · P078 Heat-shrink crimp butt splices: 1 set · P079 Ring terminals, heat-shrink, assorted 16–14 and...: 1 · P080 Tesa 51608 cloth harness tape: 5 roll · P081 Split loom / braided sleeve assortment, grommet kit,...: 1 set · P082 Cavity wax / corrosion inhibitor spray, paint pen: 1 set · P084 Adjustable plunger pin switch, 6-pack: 1 pk · P164 Comfort fuse block for O15 (5028): 1 · P172 Servo extension leads, 3-pin JR, 22 AWG, about 1 m -...: 4 · P189 Sealed inline MAXI fuse holder, 10 AWG leads, 40 A or...: 5 · P197 Rectifier diode 1N4007, pack of 10: 1 pk.
expect: Every row matches.

how: P085 Brake pedal (stop lamp) switch, without cruise - any...: 1 · P086 Ignition switch, electrical portion, 1981–83 RX-7: 1 · P113 Road-speed sensor: 1. The ignition switch must show four terminals (B, ACC, IG, ST); the brake switch two.
expect: Three parts, right terminal counts.

how: From the leaflet in each box (or the maker's page): the stud torque of the Class-T block (P047), the MRBF holder (P051), the battery post clamps (P095), the busbar (P007), the PowerPost (P050), the MIDI holders (P053) and the relay sockets' screws. Write part id, which stud, the figure and its unit.
expect: One figure per stud, written down.
caution: These figures are not in the record until you enter them: E8 to E11 torque to them.

do: Set aside anything short or wrong
how: Leave it sealed; photograph label and packing slip; note the row id and the count; contact the seller.
expect: A list of shortfalls, or none.

how: Tick D1; enter shortfalls and the torque figures as notes in the app.
expect: D1 done; D2, D3 and D4 can start.

do: Clear the bench and take metal off your hands
how: Battery on a wooden or plastic surface. Rings and watch off. Keep each post covered until its clamp goes on.
expect: Nothing metal within reach of both posts at once.
caution: Lithium: a tool across the two posts welds, it does not just spark.

how: One of the P095 pair onto the negative post; push it fully down the taper and tighten its pinch bolt.
expect: Clamp cannot be turned by hand.

how: The other P095 clamp onto the positive post, fully down, pinch bolt tight. Cover the negative clamp with its boot while you do it.
expect: Clamp cannot be turned by hand.

do: Load each stud with a 1/0 lug
how: Put one P098 lug (3/8 in hole, uncrimped) on each clamp's 3/8 stud with its washer and nut, as C12 will sit on the positive and C05 on the negative.
expect: Nut fully on with thread showing; the lug lies flat on the clamp.
caution: If the 3/8 hole does not fit the stud, note the stud's size: the lug order is wrong, not the stud.

do: Try the boots over the loaded terminals
how: Red boot on positive, black on negative (P094). Each must cover the clamp, the stud and the lug's barrel end.
expect: No metal visible on either terminal.

do: Lift each boot with one hand
how: Pull each boot off and push it back, one-handed, as you would at the roadside for a jump start.
expect: Each lifts and re-seats without a tool.

do: Try a lug boot on the 1/0 lug
how: Slide a P066 boot over a P098 lug's barrel as it will sit on the cable.
expect: The boot covers the lug's barrel and stud end.

how: Lay the P057 clamp across the case and hang the J-hooks or M8 bolts either side. Check it bears on the case, not on a terminal or a boot.
expect: Clamp spans the 170 mm width or the 230 mm length cleanly; the boots are clear of it.

do: Measure the height over the boots
how: Bench to the top of the fitted boots, in mm.
expect: A figure above 190 mm.

do: Strip it back, tick and note
how: Take the lugs off; leave the clamps on only if both boots stay on. Tick D2 and enter the height as a note.
expect: D2 done.

do: Open the first spare set over a tray
how: Tip the terminals of the first spare 39-way housing into the tray. Keep the two sets apart.
expect: One set in the tray.

how: The large ones fit the 2.8 mm die.
The small ones fit the 1.5 mm die.
Pin 15 takes a medium terminal the record does not name. Note whether the set holds one that is neither large nor small.
expect: Present or absent, written down.

how: Off the housing, the bag or the terminals' carrier strip: the housing's number and each terminal size's number.
expect: Up to three terminal numbers and the housing number written down.

do: Count the second set the same way
how: Large, small, any medium.
expect: 16 and 27 again.

how: "PMU SPARE SET 1" and "SET 2", with the counts on each bag.
expect: Two labelled bags.

how: Tick D3; enter counts and part numbers as a note in the app.
expect: D3 done; D4 may use spare terminals for its test crimps.

how: Hang the scale (P040) from a fixed hook. You will clamp each crimped contact in the vice or locking pliers, tie or loop the wire to the scale's hook, and pull steadily until the scale reads the pass figure. Eye protection on.
expect: Scale reads zero hanging free.
caution: A contact can release suddenly: pull away from your face.

do: Cut and strip three 16 AWG test wires
how: Three 150 mm lengths of 16 AWG GXL (grey P010, or any 16 AWG spool). Strip length: not in the record. Take it from the sheet that comes with the contact or the crimper, strip so the bare strands fill the barrel and no copper shows behind it, and write the length down.
expect: Clean strands, none cut or nicked.

do: Set the Deutsch crimper for size 16 on 16 AWG
how: P038 is a four-indent crimper for solid contacts. Its selector position and depth for a size-16 contact on 16 AWG are not in the record: use the chart that comes with the tool, and write the setting down.
expect: Setting written down.

do: Crimp three size-16 contacts on 16 AWG
how: Use spares P022 (socket) or P023 (pin). Seat the contact in the crimper, push the stripped wire fully into the barrel, hold the wire in, and close the handles until the ratchet releases.
expect: Four even indents round the barrel; no strand outside it; insulation right up to the barrel.

how: Clamp the contact, hook the wire to the scale and pull steadily to 20 lbf (9.1 kg). Hold a moment.
expect: All three hold at 20 lbf (9.1 kg) or more.
caution: One failure restarts the set of three after a setting change.

do: Size 16 on 14 AWG: crimp three and pull
how: Three 14 AWG wires (orange P012). Use the 14 AWG contacts P024 (socket) or P025 (pin), not the 16-18 AWG ones. Reset the crimper per its chart; crimp; pull to 34 lbf (15.4 kg).
expect: All three hold at 34 lbf (15.4 kg).

do: Size 12 on 12 AWG: crimp three and pull
how: Three 12 AWG wires (red P015). Contacts P026 (socket) or P027 (pin); there are five of each, so mix them. Set the crimper for size 12; crimp; pull to 45 lbf (20.4 kg).
expect: All three hold at 45 lbf (20.4 kg).

do: Try the open-barrel dies on one spare PMU terminal
how: Lay a spare small terminal in the 1.5 mm die of P039 and a spare large one in the 2.8 mm die, without wire, and close gently to see the wings roll evenly.
expect: Each terminal sits square in its die.
caution: Spare terminals are the only replacements: one of each for this trial, no more.

do: PMU small terminal on 16 AWG: crimp three and pull
how: Spare small terminals from D3's bags, 16 AWG wire, the 1.5 mm die. Strip length: not in the record. Take it from the sheet that comes with the contact or the crimper, strip so the bare strands fill the barrel and no copper shows behind it, and write the length down. Pull to 20 lbf (9.1 kg).
expect: All three hold at 20 lbf (9.1 kg); the wings are rolled into the strands, the rear wings grip the insulation.

do: PMU small terminal on 14 AWG: crimp three and pull
how: Six PMU pins (3, 4, 5, 9, 10, 11) carry 14 AWG in a small cavity. Same die; pull to 34 lbf (15.4 kg).
expect: All three hold at 34 lbf (15.4 kg).

do: PMU large terminal on 12 AWG: crimp three and pull
how: Spare large terminals, 12 AWG wire, the 2.8 mm die. Pull to 45 lbf (20.4 kg). Pin 25 carries 10 AWG (black P017): crimp one on 10 AWG as well and note what it holds - the record gives no figure for 10 AWG.
expect: Three at 45 lbf (20.4 kg) on 12 AWG; the 10 AWG figure noted.

how: Pin 15 takes a medium terminal whose part and die the record does not name. Do not crimp it by guess: note what D3 found.
expect: Nothing crimped; the gap noted.

how: Offcuts of 2 AWG cable (P061) and lugs P064. Fit the hydraulic crimper P037 with the die for 2 AWG - which die marking fits is not in the record: use the tool's chart and write it down. Strip to the depth of the lug's barrel, push the cable fully home, crimp.
expect: The lug cannot be pulled or twisted off by hand (the record gives no pull figure for a lug - confirm); no strands outside the barrel.
caution: Keep fingers out of the die: a hydraulic crimper does not stop.

do: 1/0 lug: crimp three with the 1/0 dies
how: Offcuts of 1/0 cable (P096) and lugs P098, the 1/0 die pair. Twelve lugs were bought for eight cable ends: three test crimps leave one spare.
expect: The lug cannot be pulled or twisted off by hand; the die closes fully.

do: 6 AWG lug: only if one is spare
how: The alternator cable uses four 6 AWG lugs (P065) and the order's target is four. If more than four arrived, crimp one on a P063 offcut; if not, the first real one at E10 is made with the 2 AWG test's care.
expect: One test lug, or none and a note.

do: Write the settings on the tools
how: For each combination: selector or die, depth, strip length, and the load held. Tape the note inside each crimper's case. Keep the test pieces in a labelled bag.
expect: One line per combination.

how: Tick D4; enter the settings and loads as a note in the app. Any crimper that failed is boxed for return.
expect: D4 done.

do: Lithium: cover both terminals, metal off your hands
how: Whenever the battery is in the car and you are working, both terminals are booted or taped. Rings and watches off.
expect: You can say why: a dropped tool across the posts welds.

do: Open the master disconnect before touching four things
how: The 2 AWG feed, the starter cable, the tank sender, and anything in the pop-up headlamp buckets. Every time. The disconnect is on the POSITIVE side in the cargo bin, so opening it removes supply from everything, the starter cable included.
expect: You can name the four.

do: Before the disconnect is fitted, pull the negative lug
how: Until E9 has fitted the disconnect, the way to make the car dead is to take the negative cable off the battery. Negative comes off first and goes back on last.
expect: You know which cable moves first.

do: Shut the engine down before opening the disconnect
how: The switch has no pole to shut the alternator down first. Engine off, then the switch.
expect: Order known: engine, then switch.
caution: Opening it with the engine running sends the alternator's output into the wiring with no battery to absorb it.

do: Treat every PMU output as possibly live
how: A PMU output's switch fails short, not open: an output can be live with the key out and the module asleep. The only thing that is certainly off is the master disconnect.
expect: You reach for the disconnect, not the key.

do: Keep the unfused cable to inches
how: The cable from the positive post to the disconnect cannot be protected by any fuse. The disconnect and the Class-T block sit as close to the positive post as physically possible.
expect: You know which cable has no fuse.

do: Leave the big fuses out while you build
how: The Class-T fuse (150 A) and the MRBF fuse (250 A) are not fitted until E11. The PMU's first power-up (E24) is through a 5 A fuse bridged across the Class-T block, so a short melts a 5 A fuse and not a 2 AWG cable.
expect: You know when each fuse goes in.

how: Never under the car on a jack alone. Chock the wheels: P on the automatic is not a parking brake.
expect: Stands and chocks by the car.

do: No sparks near the tank; extinguisher within reach
how: The pump and tank sender wiring run under the rear floor to the tank. No grinding, drilling or test sparks near it without looking first. The extinguisher is within reach, not in the next room.
expect: Extinguisher placed.

do: Engine running: clear of belt and fan, garage door open
how: Sleeves and leads clear of the belt, fan and pulleys. Door open: exhaust in a closed garage is carbon monoxide.
expect: Door open before any start.

how: Fingers out of the buckets whenever the motors can be powered. A stalled motor pulls 15 to 25 A.
expect: You open the disconnect before reaching into a bucket.

do: Label the factory end of every migrated circuit
how: When a circuit moves to the new harness, its factory end is labelled MIGRATED with the date and taped back.
expect: Labels and a pen in the kit.
caution: An unlabelled live wire taped behind a dash is the next fault.

do: Label every new wire at both ends the moment it is cut
how: Printed laminated tape, both ends, from / to. Never tape and marker.
expect: You label before cutting the next wire.

do: Torque every heavy connection and paint-mark it
how: Each heavy stud to its maker's figure (read at D1), marked with the paint pen after torquing.
expect: Torque notes and paint pen in the kit.

do: Keep water out of the new parts
how: Every conductor enters the PMU, the dash node and each panel from below or with a drip loop; nothing mounts in the lowest 50 mm of the footwell; the PMU's 39-way connector faces down or sideways, never up.
expect: You can say the three.

do: Never bare aluminium against a live stud; both busbars covered
how: Any aluminium panel is painted or coated; the always-hot busbar and the ground bus both carry covers.
expect: Known.

do: The car does not start, and is not driven, until the list says so
how: It runs at E12 on the new backbone, then does not start from E26 until E28 has moved the last circuit, and is not driven until the interior is back at E35.
expect: Known.

how: Tick E4 in the app.
expect: E4 done; E5 ready.

how: Use one DT06-4S plug kit (P124) that waits on the shelf for a part not fitted this build - L3-RDR's or L4-RDR's. It is the 4-way plug; its wedgelock is W4S. The record buys no spare housing, so treat it gently: it goes back in its bag.
expect: One 4-way plug and its wedgelock on the bench.

how: Two 150 mm lengths of 16 AWG, spare socket contacts P022, crimper P038 at D4's passing setting. Tug each by hand.
expect: Four even indents; neither pulls off by hand.

how: Find the numbers 1 to 4 moulded into the rear (wire side) of the plug.
expect: Cavity 1 found.

how: Take the wedgelock out. Push the contact into cavity 1 from the rear, through the seal, straight, until it clicks.
expect: A click you can feel.
caution: Pushing at an angle tears the rear seal.

how: Pull the wire firmly.
expect: The contact does not back out.

how: Push the wedgelock in from the mating face until it seats.
expect: Wedgelock seated; the contact cannot move.

do: Remove the wedgelock and the contact
how: Pull the wedgelock out with needle-nose pliers. Release the contact with the size-16 removal tool (P031 or P032) as the tool's instructions show, and draw the wire out of the rear.
expect: Contact out undamaged; the seal intact.
caution: Never pull a contact out by force without releasing it: the lock finger breaks.

how: Insert, click, tug, wedgelock, remove - ten times in all, with both removal tools.
expect: It clicks and holds on the tenth as on the first.

how: Join two 16 AWG offcuts with a heat-shrink butt splice (P078) or slide adhesive-lined shrink (P077) over a wire. Heat gun (P042) on its low setting, moving round the joint from the middle outward.
expect: Glue weeps evenly at both ends; no scorching.

how: On a 2 AWG offcut (P061): slide a boot (P066) and a length of heavy-wall adhesive shrink (from P077) on first, crimp a P064 lug with the hydraulic crimper at D4's die, shrink the heavy-wall over the barrel and the first of the insulation, then slide the boot over.
expect: Glue at both ends of the shrink; the boot covers the barrel.
caution: Boot and shrink go on the cable BEFORE the lug: they do not pass over it afterwards.

do: Put the plug kit back in its bag and tick
how: Wedgelock and plug back in the P124 bag, labelled. Tick E5.
expect: E5 done; E6 ready.

how: A TZe-FX231 cartridge (P075, 12 mm black on white, flexible-ID) into the PT-D220 (P041). Batteries or its adapter in.
expect: The printer feeds and cuts.

how: Type TEST / L0-X0 and print one.
expect: A clean 12 mm label.

do: Wrap it on a 16 AWG offcut
how: About 45 mm of label wrapped round the wire with the text outside; rub it down.
expect: The text reads along the wire.

how: A piece of clear 3/16 in heat-shrink (P076) over the label; shrink with the heat gun (P042) on low.
expect: Tube tight, text readable through it.

how: Pull the label along the wire with your fingers.
expect: It does not move.

how: One label each, the id is where it goes and the word is the label: K1 POPUP-L · K2 POPUP-R · K3 HATCH-REL · K4 FUEL-REL · K5 WIN-D-UP · K6 WIN-D-DN · K7 WIN-P-UP · K8 WIN-P-DN · K9 START · K11 HEAD-UNIT · K12 WASHER · K13 FUEL-PUMP · K14 SEAT-D · K15 SEAT-P. Whether the id is printed with the word is not in the record: printing both loses nothing.
expect: 14 labels.

how: Class-T MAIN · MRBF STARTER · F1 HEAD-UNIT · F2 DIAG · F3 SWITCH · F8 WIN-DRV · F9 WIN-PASS · F12 INTERIOR · F13 — · F14 MIRROR-HEAT · F15 ALT-EXCITE · F16 DISPLAY · F17 START-RLY · F18 ALTERNATOR · F19 COURTESY · F20 WIDEBAND · F21 KICK-DOWN · F22 DCU-CONST · F23 WAKE · F24 LIGHT-SW · F5 SENSOR-2 · F25 SEAT-D-HEAT · F26 SEAT-P-HEAT · F27 SEAT-D-COOL · F28 SEAT-P-COOL · F29 DCU-CMF · F30 BLOCK-A-FEED · F31 K11-FEED · F32 BLOCK-B-FEED · F33 RELEASE · F34 AMP · F35 SEAT-D · F36 SEAT-P · F37 POPUP-CMD.
expect: 34 labels; F13's reads as an empty position.

how: Stick each on a card or backing sheet in table order, marked RELAYS and FUSES. They go on the dash node at E14 and at the sill and bay as each part is fitted.
expect: One card, all labels on it.

how: Tick E6.
expect: E6 done; E7 ready.

do: Lay out the kit and print the labels
how: Resistor kit P069, diodes 1N4148 (P161), 1N4007 (P197), 16 AWG grey offcuts (P010) cut into 4 in (100 mm) leads, adhesive shrink (P077). Print one label per part: the switch and the position, e.g. the key switch's three read A16 ACC, A16 IG, A16 ST.
expect: Labels printed; leads cut.

do: Make one part, the pattern for all
how: Measure the bare resistor first. Solder a 4 in lead to each end, slide heat-shrink over the whole resistor and both joints, shrink, and wrap the label on one lead.
expect: A resistor with two insulated leads and a label.
caution: Hot iron and molten solder: eye protection, and let the joint cool before the shrink.

how: Meter on ohms across the two lead ends. Write the reading on the bag with the label's text.
expect: Within 1 % of the marked value.

how: 33 kΩ labelled ACC · 15 kΩ labelled IG · 6.8 kΩ labelled ST.
expect: Three bags.

how: 33 kΩ PARK · 15 kΩ HEAD · 8.2 kΩ DIMMER-HI · 3.3 kΩ PASS.
expect: Four bags; the PASS bag marked "waits on CK17".

how: 1.8 kΩ LEFT · 10 kΩ RIGHT · 47 kΩ OFF.
expect: Three bags.

how: 4.7 kΩ HIGH · 10 kΩ LOW · 18 kΩ INT · 47 kΩ OFF.
expect: Four bags.

do: Wiper WASH leg: confirm, then make
how: The ladders table gives 470 Ω in series with a 1N4148; the older cavity row gives 1.8 kΩ with a 1N5819, band toward the contact. Check the app for which stands before soldering. Resistor and diode in series on one lead, under one piece of shrink, the diode's band end marked on the outside.
expect: One bag, or none and a note.
caution: A diode soldered the wrong way round reads as a switch never pressed.

do: Brake and wiper park (A3): three parts
how: 4.7 kΩ BRAKE (pedal switch) · 12 kΩ PARKED (wiper motor terminal L) · 47 kΩ A3 BASELINE (front ground at the L2-S plug).
expect: Three bags; the baseline bag marked "not before CK12".

how: 4.7 kΩ HAZARD · 47 kΩ A8 BASELINE (column ground at the hazard switch) · 8.2 kΩ HORN. The wink resistors are on the plate board: not made here.
expect: Three bags; the baseline bag marked "not before CK12".

do: Gear selector switch (A4, A5): four parts
how: 8.2 kΩ A4 P/N (lead to terminal BY) · 47 kΩ A4 BASELINE · 8.2 kΩ A5 REVERSE (lead to terminal GY) · 47 kΩ A5 BASELINE.
expect: Four bags.

how: 24 kΩ + 1N4148 DRIVER · 8.2 kΩ + 1N4148 PASSENGER, each resistor and diode in series with the diode's anode (the end without the band) toward the splice · 47 kΩ A6 BASELINE (sill splice to sill ground).
expect: Three bags; the baseline bag marked "not before CK12".
caution: Mark the band end on the outside of the shrink.

how: Two 1N4007 (P197), each on two leads under shrink, labelled RY DRIVER and RY PASSENGER, the anode end marked: the anode goes to the lamp's RY wire.
expect: Two bags.

do: Check each diode part with the meter
how: Meter on diode test: one way reads about 0.5 to 0.7 V, the other way open. Through a resistor-and-diode part use ohms both ways: one way the resistor's value or a little more, the other way open.
expect: Every diode part conducts one way only.

do: Count the bags against the list
how: Key 3 · light 4 · turn 3 · wiper 4 (+ WASH) · brake and park 3 · hazard and horn 3 · gear selector 4 · doors 3 · lamp diodes 2.
expect: 29 bags, or 30 with the WASH leg.

how: Tick E7. Note the WASH leg's state in the app if it was left.
expect: E7 done; E8 ready.

how: Key out, wheels chocked, car in P. Rings and watch off. If you go under for the starter cable, the car is on jack stands.
expect: Car cannot roll; nothing switched on.
caution: Never under the car on a jack alone.

do: Photograph the factory battery and both cables
how: In the engine bay: the battery, each clamp, every lead on each clamp, the positive cable's run to the starter and to the fusible-link block, the negative cable to its ground bolt.
expect: Each cable's two ends on a photo.

how: Loosen the negative clamp and lift it off the post; tuck it where it cannot spring back.
expect: Negative clamp off and clear.
caution: Negative first: with it off, a spanner touching the body from the positive post makes no spark.

do: Disconnect the positive cable and lift the battery out
how: Positive clamp off. Undo the factory hold-down and lift the battery out upright.
expect: Battery on the floor, away from the car.
caution: A lead-acid battery is heavy and holds acid: lift with both hands, keep it upright.

do: Write down how the positive cable is built
how: The positive cable (Mazda 8872-67-250B, clips 1011-67-291A and 1011-67-293) goes to the starter's main stud and feeds the fusible-link block X-07. Note exactly how the link block gets its supply: a ring under the clamp bolt, a branch crimped into the cable, or a separate lead. Note its wire size if printed.
expect: A sketch or photo and one sentence.
caution: E11 lands this feed on the new backbone: without this note you will be guessing then.

do: Write down where the negative cable went
how: Follow the negative cable (Mazda 8871-67-260A) to its bolt: body or engine, and any second small lead from the clamp to the body.
expect: The ground point named and photographed.

how: Undo the nut on the starter's main B+ stud, lift the cable's ring off, and put the nut back finger-tight. The small wire on the starter's S terminal (factory BW) stays. Free the cable from its clips. Leave the fusible-link block and its three links on the car: tape and label its battery-side lead "MAIN FEED - TO POST (E11)".
expect: Cable out; link block untouched; its feed lead insulated and labelled.
caution: Do not cut a fusible link or its wire.

how: Unbolt it at its ground point and take it out. If a small body lead shared the clamp, tape and label it "FACTORY GROUND - TO FRONT STAR (E11)".
expect: Cable out.

do: Bag and label the factory parts
how: Battery cables, clamps and hold-down in a bag marked "factory battery cables - not reused".
expect: One labelled bag.

how: Before the Ionic goes near the car: red and black boots (P094) on its posts or post clamps.
expect: No metal showing on either terminal.
caution: Lithium: a tool across the posts welds.

how: From the P092 stock (3 to 4 mm aluminium or steel), to the outline of the M-4 cardboard mock-up. Deburr every edge. If it is aluminium, paint it (P093).
expect: A plate matching the mock-up, no sharp edges.

do: Look under the floor, then mark the holes
how: Set the mock-up in the passenger-side cargo bin where M-4 put the battery. Go under the car and look at what is beneath that floor: the tank, the pump and sender wiring, brake and fuel lines. Mark the hold-down holes only where the plate sits flat and nothing is behind.
expect: Hole positions marked with clear space under each.
caution: Drilling into a fuel or brake line, or the tank, is the worst mistake of the weekend. No sparks near the tank.

do: Drill and bolt the hold-down through floor and plate
how: Drill for the M8 hardware. From above: the hold-down's J-hooks or bolts (P057, M8 grade-8) through the floor; beneath: the backing plate, a fender washer and a nyloc nut on each. Torque is not in the record: tighten firmly and evenly, and note it.
expect: Plate tight against the underside; bolts cannot turn.
caution: Never through sheet metal alone: the plate must be under every bolt.

how: Lower the Ionic (170 x 230 x 190 mm) into place as mocked up, with a post reachable by hand for a jump start with the boots on.
expect: Battery flat on the bin floor, posts reachable.

how: Clamp over the case, clear of both terminals and boots; tighten its nuts evenly.
expect: Clamp bears on the case only.

how: Push and pull the battery forward, back, each side and up.
expect: It does not move at all.
caution: If it shifts, it is not done: a loose battery with live terminals is a projectile in a crash.

do: Leave it unconnected, booted, and tick
how: Both boots on. No cable goes on the Ionic this weekend. Tick E8 and enter the notes from steps 5 and 6.
expect: E8 done; E9 ready.

how: Both battery terminals booted, nothing connected to the battery, rings and watch off. The disconnect, when fitted, stays OFF; the Class-T fuse stays in its box.
expect: Battery isolated.
caution: Lithium: one slip with a spanner across the posts welds.

how: Blue Sea 9003e (P049), where the M-4 mock-up put it: within reach from the open hatch, inches from the positive post. Its fasteners are not in the record: note them. Turn it OFF.
expect: Switch solid, reachable from the hatch, OFF.

how: Blue Sea 5007100 (P047) beside the disconnect, as close to the positive post as physically possible. Leave the 150 A fuse (P048) out; keep its cover to hand.
expect: Block solid, inches from the post, no fuse in it.

how: On bare structural metal within reach of the negative post (C05 is estimated at 3 ft). Grind to bright metal. Fit a 3/8 in stainless stud (P058) with a star washer (P059) biting the bare metal; how the stud is fixed through the panel is not in the record: note it. Torque it, then cavity wax (P082) round the stud-to-body joint.
expect: A solid stud on bright metal, waxed at its base.
caution: Look behind the panel before drilling: the tank and its wiring are under the rear floor.

do: Lay C12 in place and mark it
how: Hold the 1/0 red cable (P096) from the positive clamp's 3/8 stud to the disconnect's INPUT stud along the path it will take, with a gentle bend and no strain. Mark the cut. The table's 1.0 ft is an estimate: the length is what the two studs need, kept to inches.
expect: A cut mark; the real length written down.
caution: This cable has no fuse: shorter is safer, and nothing may chafe it.

how: Cut. Slide on a red boot (P066) and a length of heavy-wall shrink (from P077) for each end FIRST. Strip each end to the depth of the lug's barrel. Fit a 1/0 lug (P098, 3/8 in hole) fully home and crimp with the hydraulic crimper (P037) and the 1/0 dies as at D4. Shrink the heavy-wall over barrel and insulation until glue shows at both ends; slide the boots up. Label both ends C12, from / to.
expect: Two lugs that cannot be twisted by hand; glue at both ends of each shrink; both lug faces lie flat on their studs with the cable relaxed.
caution: Boot and shrink on before the second lug. Fingers out of the die.

how: 2 AWG red (P061) from the disconnect's OUTPUT stud to the Class-T block's input stud; table estimate 1.0 ft. Mark in place, cut, boots and shrink on, lugs P064 with the hole each stud needs, crimp with the 2 AWG die, shrink, label C01.
expect: As C12.

how: 1/0 black (P097) from the negative clamp's 3/8 stud straight to the rear ground stud; table estimate 3 ft. Mark in place, cut, black boots and shrink on, P098 lugs (3/8 in hole), crimp, shrink, label C05.
expect: As C12.

how: One end on the positive clamp's stud (lift the red boot, refit it over the stack), the other on the disconnect's INPUT stud. Torque each to the maker's figure you read at D1; paint-mark each nut.
expect: Both nuts torqued and marked; the post boot back on over the lug.
caution: The INPUT stud is now live. The switch stays OFF.

how: One lug on the disconnect's OUTPUT stud - snug only for now, because the MRBF holder stacks on top of it at E10 - and the other on the Class-T block's input stud, torqued to Blue Sea's figure and paint-marked.
expect: C01 in place; the Class-T end torqued and marked.

do: Bolt C05 at the stud only
how: C05's lug on the rear ground stud over a star washer, nut snug (the cranking return C11 joins it at E10). Leave its battery end OFF the negative clamp: boot it, tape it and tie it back.
expect: Negative cable fixed at the stud, free and insulated at the battery.
caution: The negative lug stays off until E11: that is what keeps the car dead.

do: Check through the switch with the meter
how: Meter on ohms, one probe on the positive clamp's stud (under the boot), the other on the Class-T block's input stud. Switch ON, then OFF.
expect: ON: continuity, under 1 ohm. OFF: open circuit.

how: Switch OFF. Class-T fuse out. Both post boots on. Tools out of the bin.
expect: Nothing live beyond the disconnect's input stud.

how: Tick E9; enter the three cut lengths and the torques used as a note in the app.
expect: E9 done; E10 ready.

how: Disconnect OFF, Class-T fuse out, C05's battery end still off and insulated, post boots on. Car on jack stands, wheels chocked, engine cold.
expect: Car dead and solid on its stands.
caution: Never under the car on a jack alone.

do: Fit the MRBF holder on the disconnect's output stud
how: Blue Sea 5191 holder (P051) onto the OUTPUT stud, on top of C01's lug. Torque to Blue Sea's figure (read at D1); paint-mark. Do NOT fit the 250 A fuse (P052).
expect: Holder solid on the stud with C01 under it; no fuse.
caution: The row's note says "on the positive post": the tables put it on the disconnect's output stud, so the disconnect also kills the starter cable.

do: Lay the three tunnel routes with string
how: From the cargo bin forward through the tunnel: one string to the starter's main stud, one to the engine block, one to the dash-node position. Follow the path the cables will take, away from the exhaust, the propeller shaft and the shifter. Measure each string.
expect: Three measured lengths written down - they replace the table's estimates of 18, 18 and 16 ft.
caution: Heat and moving parts: nothing heavy may touch the exhaust or the shaft.

how: 1/0 red (P096) off the reel along its string from the MRBF holder to the starter. Leave it long at both ends. Loom it (P081); a grommet wherever it passes through metal.
expect: Red 1/0 from bin to starter, in loom, uncut at the starter end.

do: Pull C11, the cranking return, beside it
how: 1/0 black (P097) from the rear ground stud to the engine block, in the same run as C04. Loom; grommets.
expect: Black 1/0 beside the red, bin to block.

do: Pull C03, the PMU feed, with its pull string
how: 2 AWG red (P061) from the Class-T block's output stud through the tunnel to the dash-node position. Loom its full length; grommets at every pass-through. Lay the pull string (from P081) beside it the whole way and tie off both ends.
expect: Red 2 AWG from bin to dash, and a string beside it you can pull from either end.
caution: The string must be in before the console goes back: it is how later wires get through.

how: P-clips (P081) every 12 in along each cable, onto existing or new fixings; no cable hangs or can move against an edge.
expect: A clip every 12 in; nothing sags.

do: Terminate C04 at the bin and bolt it on
how: Cut to length at the MRBF holder. Boot and heavy-wall shrink on first; P098 lug with the 5/16 in hole; crimp (1/0 dies), shrink, label C04. Bolt it to the holder's fuse stud; torque; paint-mark.
expect: C04 on the MRBF holder.

do: Terminate C04 at the starter and bolt it on
how: Cut at the starter's main B+ stud. Boot and shrink on; a P098 lug whose hole matches the stud (measured at CK24); crimp, shrink, label. Fit it on the main stud where the factory cable was; nut torqued to the maker's figure - not in the record, confirm; paint-mark; boot over.
expect: C04 on the starter's main stud; the small S-terminal wire untouched.
caution: The starter stud is live whenever the disconnect is ON and the MRBF is in: boot it.

how: Engine end: a P098 lug (3/8 in hole) on a clean, bare threaded boss on the block - which bolt is not in the record: note it. Bin end: a P098 lug onto the rear ground stud on top of C05's. Boots, shrink, labels as before.
expect: C11 bolted to the block and to the rear stud.

do: Torque and wax the rear ground stud
how: With C05 and C11 both on it: torque, paint-mark, cavity wax (P082) over the whole joint. The 10 AWG stud-to-chassis wire G23 is in the grounds table but not in this row's note: fit it now with a P079 ring if you wish, or leave it for the rear leg, and note which.
expect: Rear stud finished and waxed.

do: Mount the temporary post and land C03
how: Blue Sea 2003 PowerPost (P050, 3/8 in stud, insulated) where the dash node will go (from M-1). Terminate C03 with P064 lugs: one on the Class-T block's OUTPUT stud, one on the post. Torque both to Blue Sea's figures; paint-mark; cover on the post.
expect: C03 from Class-T output to the post; the post covered.

how: On the radiator support: grind to bare metal, 3/8 in stainless stud (P058), star washer (P059), torque, cavity wax (P082).
expect: Stud on bright metal, waxed.

do: Run the front star's 10 AWG wire
how: 10 AWG black GXL (P017), about 2 ft, from the front star stud to a second bare-metal body bolt. A heat-shrink ring (P079, 12-10 AWG) at each end, crimped with P171, shrunk. Label G05.
expect: Stud bonded to the body by a second path.

do: Fit the engine block to chassis strap, C06
how: 2 AWG black (P062), 24 in or less, P064 lugs, from a bare boss on the block to bare metal on the chassis; which bolts is not in the record: note them. Boots and shrink; torque; wax the chassis end.
expect: A short black strap, block to body, both ends on bright metal.

do: Mount the two MIDI holders beside the starter stud
how: Two Blue Sea 7720 blocks (P053) on M6 fixings near the starter's main stud, covers to hand. Label them F17 START-RLY and F18 ALTERNATOR (labels from E6).
expect: Two holders mounted and labelled.

how: 6 AWG red (P063) in two pieces with P065 lugs: starter main stud to F18's one stud, and F18's other stud to the alternator's B stud - about 4 ft in all. Fit the 100 A fuse (P055, Blue Sea 5256) in F18; cover on. The factory WR wire on the alternator's B stud: the row does not say to remove it and the factory harness is not migrated until E28 - leave it on the stud and note it.
expect: Alternator B to F18 to starter stud in 6 AWG; 100 A fuse in; cover on.
caution: A 150 A MIDI must not go here: 6 AWG needs the 100 A.

how: F17's holder is fitted and empty of wires. Its 30 A fuse (P054, Blue Sea 5250) stays in its bag, taped to the holder, until K9 is wired at E27.
expect: F17 holder mounted, nothing on it.

do: Check with the meter, everything dead
how: Meter on ohms. Rear ground stud to engine block: continuity, under 1 ohm. Engine block to chassis: under 1 ohm. Class-T output stud to the temporary post: under 1 ohm. MRBF holder's fuse stud to the starter's main stud: under 1 ohm. The temporary post to chassis: open circuit.
expect: Four continuities and one open.
caution: An open post-to-chassis reading matters: anything else means C03 is chafed through somewhere.

how: Disconnect still OFF, both big fuses still out. Tick E10; enter the lengths, bolts and torques as a note.
expect: E10 done; E11 ready.

do: Check the car is still dead
how: Disconnect OFF; Class-T block and MRBF holder empty; C05's battery end off and insulated; post boots on.
expect: Nothing live beyond the disconnect's input stud.

do: Find the fusible-link block and its supply lead
how: Block X-07: one black link (the 1.25 sq MAIN) between two brown 0.3 sq links - by the 1985 manual at the front left suspension tower, confirm. Its battery-side lead is the one you taped and labelled "MAIN FEED - TO POST" at E8.
expect: Block found; three links intact; the feed lead in your hand.
caution: Do not bypass, shorten or replace a fusible link.

do: Join the feed lead to the temporary post
how: The lead must reach the PowerPost's 3/8 in stud at the dash-node position with all three links still between the post and the factory harness. The record does not say what conductor covers that distance: if the lead reaches, fit a ring (P079, crimped with P171) and bolt it on the post; if it does not, stop here and raise it in the app with the distance and the lead's wire size.
expect: The factory feed on the post, links in series - or a note raised and the row left open.
caution: An unfused extension between the post and the links would be protected only by the 150 A Class-T: do not improvise one.

do: Move the factory main ground to the front star
how: The lead you labelled "FACTORY GROUND - TO FRONT STAR" at E8 - the factory negative cable's connection to the body - lands on the front star stud with a ring over a star washer. If the factory negative went only to the engine and no body lead exists, note that: the block is already bonded by C06 and C11. Leave the harness's own ground bolts X-13, X-14 and X-15 where they are.
expect: Factory ground on the front star, or a note that there is none.

do: Go round every heavy joint once more
how: Every stud from the bin to the bay: nut torqued, paint mark present, boot or cover on. No tool left in the bin or the bay.
expect: Every joint marked; nothing loose.

how: One 150 A fuse (P048) into the Class-T block; nuts to Blue Sea's figure; cover on. The second fuse goes with the car's spares.
expect: Fuse in, cover on.

how: The 250 A MRBF (P052) into the 5191 holder on the disconnect's output stud, with C04's lug on the holder's fuse stud; torque; cover on.
expect: Fuse in; the starter cable now fused.

how: Check the positive clamp, its stud nut and boot. Then put C05's lug on the negative clamp's stud, torque it, and boot it.
expect: Both terminals connected and booted. No spark: the disconnect is OFF.
caution: If anything sparks as the negative goes on, the disconnect is not OFF or something bypasses it: take the lug straight off.

how: Stand clear of the bin, switch ON, and watch and smell for ten seconds.
expect: No spark, no smoke, no smell.
caution: Hand on the switch: OFF at the first sign of anything.

do: Read the post with the meter
how: Meter on DC volts: red on the temporary post's stud, black on the front star stud.
expect: The pack's voltage, about 13 V - the same as the app will show.

how: Key to ON (do not crank). The factory circuits that worked before work now: try the hazards, the horn, the lamps you can still reach. Key off.
expect: Factory circuits live, as before, on the new backbone.
caution: Do not start it today: the cluster is unplugged.

how: On the phone, open the Ionic app and connect to the pack by Bluetooth. Do not accept or start any firmware update.
expect: The pack appears with live readings.

how: From the app, with the disconnect ON and the key off: pack voltage (E45, in V), state of charge (E46, in %), pack temperature (E47, in C).
expect: Three figures written down.

how: Disconnect OFF if you are leaving the car. Tick E11, then enter the three readings in E45, E46 and E47.
expect: E11 done; E12 ready.

do: Make the garage safe to run an engine
how: Door open. Wheels chocked, car in P. Leads, rags and tools clear of the belt, fan and pulleys. Extinguisher within reach.
expect: Fresh air and a clear engine bay.
caution: A running engine in a closed garage is carbon monoxide.

how: The cluster was unplugged at S1, not cut: plug its connectors back in and rest it where it cannot short on bare metal.
expect: Cluster connected and supported.

how: Master disconnect ON. Key to ON: the cluster's warning lamps light.
expect: Cluster alive.

how: Clip the jumper lead to one meter probe so the meter can sit in the cargo bin with one probe on a battery post and the other reaching the starter stud and the engine block.
expect: Meter reads the pack voltage, post to post, through the long lead.

how: Assistant turns the key to START in P. Let it idle and warm.
expect: It starts and idles.
caution: Hands, hair and leads away from the belt and fan.

do: Read the charging voltage at 2,000 rpm - this is E42
how: Engine warm. Meter on DC volts, red probe on the battery + post, black on the - post (lift the boots). Assistant holds 2,000 rpm on the tachometer. Read with the headlights off, then with headlights and blower on (if the blower cannot be switched with the dash out, take the headlights reading and note it).
expect: 13.8 to 14.6 V, and never above 14.6 V.
caution: Above 14.6 V: back to idle and stop - do not keep charging the lithium pack at that voltage.

do: If it does not charge, stop here
how: A reading that stays at the resting pack voltage, or falls, means no charge. Shut down. The alternator or its excitation is at fault; excitation is rebuilt at E28. Enter the figure in E42 anyway and note it.
expect: Either a charging figure, or the engine off and a note.

how: Key off. Leave the disconnect ON for the next two tests.
expect: Engine stopped.

do: Cranking drop, positive side - this is E43
how: Red probe on the battery + POST itself (not the clamp), black probe on the starter's main B+ stud through the long lead. Assistant holds the key at START for about three seconds; read the meter while it cranks (use min/max hold if you have it).
expect: Under 0.5 V while cranking.
caution: The engine may fire: stay clear of the belt and fan at the starter.

do: Cranking drop, negative side - this is E44
how: Red probe on bare metal of the engine block, black probe on the battery - POST itself. Crank again for about three seconds and read.
expect: Under 0.5 V while cranking.

do: Run it and try every factory circuit
how: Start again. Idle, then rev. Work each factory circuit: headlamps and pop-ups, park and tail lamps, turn signals and hazards, brake lamps, horn, wipers and washer, blower, rear defogger, the gauges.
expect: Everything behaves exactly as it did before the backbone changed.
caution: Fingers out of the pop-up buckets.

how: Key off and engine stopped FIRST, then the master disconnect OFF.
expect: Car dead.
caution: Never open the disconnect with the engine running.

how: Tick E12 with the charging voltage as its value. Enter E42, E43 and E44 in their rows.
expect: E12 done: the car runs on the new backbone. No driving until E35.

do: Set the meter at the battery
how: During E12 step 6. Meter on DC volts. Lift both post boots. Red probe on the + post, black on the - post.
expect: The pack voltage with the engine idling.

how: Assistant holds 2,000 rpm on the tachometer, headlights off. Wait for the figure to settle.
caution: Above 14.6 V: back to idle and shut down.

do: Read at 2,000 rpm with headlights and blower on
how: Same probes, headlights on and the blower on.
expect: 13.8 to 14.6 V, at or a little under the first reading.

how: Boots back on. Enter the higher reading in E42, in V; note both.
expect: E42 holds one figure.

how: During E12 step 9. Red probe on the battery + POST itself, under the boot - not on the clamp. Black probe, through the long lead, on the starter's main B+ stud.
expect: About 0 V with nothing cranking.

how: Assistant holds the key at START for about three seconds. Read the meter while the starter turns (or its max hold afterwards).
expect: Under 0.5 V.
caution: Stay clear of the belt and fan: the engine may fire.

how: Enter the reading in E43, in V.
expect: E43 holds one figure.

how: During E12 step 10. Black probe on the battery - POST itself, under the boot. Red probe, through the long lead, on bare metal of the engine block - not a bracket, not the strap.
expect: About 0 V with nothing cranking.

how: Assistant holds the key at START for about three seconds. Read while the starter turns.
expect: Under 0.5 V.
caution: Stay clear of the belt and fan.

how: Enter the reading in E44, in V.
expect: E44 holds one figure.

do: Open the app at the pack
how: At E11 step 13, disconnect ON, key off. The app's main screen for the pack.
expect: Live readings.

how: The total pack voltage, not a cell voltage.
expect: A figure near 13 V.

how: Enter it in E45, in V.
expect: E45 holds one figure.

how: At E11 step 13, on the same screen as the voltage.
expect: A percentage.

do: Check it is enough to start on
how: The record sets no figure. If the app shows the pack low, charge it before E12.
expect: Charged enough, or on charge.
caution: Only a lithium (LiFePO4) profile charger.

how: Enter it in E46, in %.
expect: E46 holds one figure.

how: At E11 step 13, on the app's pack screen.
expect: A temperature near the garage's.

how: The row's unit is C. From Fahrenheit: subtract 32, multiply by 5, divide by 9.
expect: A figure in C.

how: Enter it in E47, in C.
expect: E47 holds one figure.
